title: Dual-molecule enhanced MXene films for high specific capacitance in supercapacitors
authors: Shiben Jiang, Yijie Shi, Linghong Lu, Changrui Hua, Yan Song, Jun Li
abstract: In order to solve the problem of restacking the two-dimensional layered structure of MXene without causing a decrease in its conductivity, electrochemical performance, and flexibility, this study innovatively proposes a dual-molecule synergistic strategy utilizing polypyrrole (ppy) and 4-O-TEMPO (TEMPO = 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidinyl-1-oxyl) to achieve high-capacitance MXene films. In this strategy, 4-O-TEMPO anchors to the surface and edges of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets through hydrogen and covalent bonds, with its nitroxide radicals participating in redox reactions to contribute additional pseudocapacitance. Additionally, ppy enhances the conductivity of the composite film by shortening the electron transport path and prevents MXene from excessive oxidized by 4-O-TEMPO. This bimolecular strategy effectively alleviates interlayer stacking in MXene while maintaining its conductivity and flexibility. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Ti3C2O2 has stable interactions with 4-O-TEMPO, and the ternary system demonstrates excellent electronic and ion transport properties. As a result, the ppy MXene 4-O-TEMPO (pMT) electrode achieves a specific capacitance of 530 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 and retains 300 F g 1 at 50 A g 1. Additionally, the asymmetric supercapacitor reaches 23.8 Wh kg 1 energy density at 300.2 W kg 1 power density.
conclusion: In conclusion, we propose a new strategy for the synergistic modification of the surface of MXene nanosheets by ppy and 4-O-TEMPO dual-molecule, where self-supported film electrodes can be formed by vacuum filtration. Among them, 4-O-TEMPO can not only form hydrogen bonds with the surface of MXene, but more importantly, it is covalently attached to the edge of Ti3 C2 Tx through Ti-O. The nitroxide radicals provided by 4-O-TEMPO participate in the redox reaction, which can provide more pseudocapacitance. On the other hand, ppy is arranged on the surface of MXene through abundant hydrogen bonding interactions, which not only compensates for the low conductivity of nitroxide radicals, but also serves as a barrier to protect MXene from over-oxidation during the grafting process of 4-O-TEMPO. In addition, DFT elucidated the formation of an internal electric field at the interface of the dual-molecule with MXene, which accelerates the electron transport. As a result, the pMT electrode has a high specific capacitance of 530 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 and still maintains 300 F g 1 at 50 A g 1 , exhibiting excellent rate performance. In addition, the constructed pMT TPC ASC are able to achieve a maximum energy density of 23.8 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 300.2 W kg 1 . The present work not only successfully integrates the unique advantages of dual-molecule with the properties of MXene, but also provides a new perspective on the surface modification strategy of MXene. title: Multiscale porous structured MXene: Synthesis, design and applications in batteries and supercapacitors
authors: Chen Chen, Xincao Tang, Mengjie Wang, Yanan Ma, Siliang Wang, Yang Yue
abstract: The porous structure of 2D MXene play a critical role in addressing ion transport and kinetic limitations of traditional electrodes, enabling significant improvements of electrochemical performance for energy storage applications. In contrast to previous reviews those have focused only on a specific type of pore structure, this review systematically summarizes the construction strategies and structural properties of micropores, mesopores, and macropores of MXene electrodes, and outlines their evolution from single-scale regulation to multiscale synergistic coupling enhancement. On the basis of a brief review of the synthesis methods and physicochemical properties of MXene, we detail the introduced key structural parameters (e.g. pore size, pore geometry), and elucidate their synergistic effect on ion electron transport pathways, active site exposure, and electrolyte wettability. Furthermore, this review analyzes the unique roles and synergies of different pore scales in energy storage mechanisms, and discusses the application progress of multiscale porous MXene in lithium-ion batteries, zinc-ion batteries, supercapacitors, and so on. This review aims to provide practical insights into the rational design and application of multiscale porous MXene, thereby promoting advancements in energy storage technologies and related fields.
conclusion: Summary and outlook Summary Research advances in multiscale pore structures of 2D MXene provide important opportunities to regulate the diffusion behavior and chemical kinetics of active materials, thereby significantly advancing the development of energy storage devices. By scientifically designing and controlling pore parameters (such as pore size, pore orientation, shape and porosity), can effectively enhance the efficiency of ion electron transport and promote the permeation of different electrolytes through various pores, thus optimizing the electrochemical performance of MXene. Particularly, the synergistic effects across multiple pore scales, the quantitative regulation of pore sizes from micropores, mesopores and macropores, and the precise control of pore geometries have been proven to be key strategies in achieving high-performance MXene electrode. Therefore, fully utilizing interdisciplinary knowledge in materials science, chemistry, and physics to precisely design and control pore parameters further advances the application of multiscale pore MXene, which will offer a more comprehensive solution to improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage devices. Outlook Multiscale porous MXene have demonstrated impressive performance in laboratory-scale energy storage applications, but still faces several unresolved issues. To bridge the gap between academic innovation and industrial translation, key scientific and engineering challenges must be addressed. 1. Fluoride-dependent synthesis methods: Currently, large-scale fabrication of MXene still relies heavily on fluorinated etchants (e.g., HF, LiF HCl), which raise environmental, safety, and cost issues, limiting industrial scalability. 2. Lack of electrolyte-pore matching principles: How different pore sizes (and their hierarchical combinations) interact with various electrolytes, including differing in ionic size, solvation shell, or charge has not been systematically established, leading to deteriorated electrochemical performance. 3. Unclear structure-performance relationship of multiscale pores: The optimal electrochemical performance and spatial distribution of micropores, mesopores, and macropores remain poorly understood, particularly regarding their integrated effect onion transport, mechanical integrity, and volumetric energy density. To address these challenges, we make several recommendations: 1. Green and scalable synthesis: Fluoride-free routes (e.g., molten salt etching [ 34 ] and electrochemical exfoliation) should be developed to enable safer, environmentally friendly, and industrially viable MXene production. 2. Systematic electrolyte pore compatibility studies: Future research should explore how pore size and hierarchy affect ion accessibility in electrolytes with different ionic radius, solvation shells, and charges. Understanding these interactions is crucial for tailoring MXene structures to diverse electrolyte systems and maximizing charge transport efficiency [ 339 ]. 3. Apply bio-inspired and data-driven design strategies ( Fig. 11 ): Principles derived from biological systems, such as Murray s Law and Fibonacci sequence-based distributions [ 340 342 ], can offer useful guidance for optimizing hierarchical pore design. In parallel, deep learning algorithms and data-driven models should be applied to predict ideal pore configurations and accelerate the design of high-performance MXene-based electrodes [ 343 347 ].

title: Self-standing porous MXene film via in situ formed microgel induced by 2- methylimidazole for high rate supercapacitor
authors: Sai Yan, Chenjing Shi, Zhen Tian, Dan Li, Yanjun Chen, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene has been considered a potential supercapacitor electrode material on account of its fast electron transfer performance, large volume pseudocapacitance, excellent hydrophilicity and mechanical properties. However, the serious stacking of MXene nanosheets reduced the exposed active sites and hindered diffusion of ions, leading to bad electrochemical property. Here, we report a strategy to transform MXene nanosheets into 3D MXene microgels induced by 2-methylimidazole. Benefitting from the existence of microgels, it facilitates the rapid vacuum filtration to prepare the porous MXene film, thus enhancing the ion transfer efficiency. Furthermore, 2-methylimidazole can also act as an intercalated agent to increase the layer spacing of MXene nanosheets. Therefore, the as-prepared porous MXene film demonstrates a superior rate capacity, and its capacitance reaches 223.4 F g 1 at the scan rates of 1000 mV s 1. Moreover, the assembled MXene AC asymmetrical supercapacitor displays a 16.88 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 799 W kg 1, and maintains 13.11 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 8 kW kg 1. This work develops a simple way to prepare the porous MXene film for supercapacitors with excellent electrochemical performance.
conclusion: In summary, we purpose a new strategy to prepare the self-standing porous MXene film via the in-situ formation MXene microgel induced by 2-MeIM and vacuum filtration. The hydrogen ion released from the deprotonation of 2-MeIM and hydron bonding interaction between 2-MeIM and MXene nanosheets break the electrostatic balance of MXene nanosheets, resulting in the assembly of MXene nanosheets into 3D MXene microgel. The formed MXene microgel in MXene suspension not only reduces the time of vacuum filtration to prepare the porous M-MXene-5 film but also facilitates the electrolyte ions transport. Meanwhile, 2-methylimidazole acts as an intercalated agent to increase the layer spacing of MXene. As a result, the M-MXene film has an excellent rate performance, demonstrating the specific capacitance of 223.4 F g 1 even at a scan rate of 1000 mV s 1 . Moreover, the assembled M-MXene-5 AC ASC device displays 16.88 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 799 W kg 1 , and maintains 13.11 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 8 kW kg 1 . Meanwhile, the ASC device shows the exceptional cycling stability with the capacitance retention of 90.4 after 10 000 cycles. This work opens a new way to prepare the porous MXene film with excellent electrochemical properties for high rate supercapacitors.

title: Advancements and approaches in developing MXene-based hybrid composites for improved supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Thibeorchews Prasankumar, Kaaviah Manoharan, N.K. Farhana, Shahid Bashir, K. Ramesh, S. Ramesh, Vigna K. Ramachandaramurthy
abstract: The rapid increase in population and widespread use of energy-consuming technologies are contributing to a substantial increase in the world s energy consumption. Supercapacitors have recently become a more desirable alternative due to their quick charging and discharging times, high power densities, and extended cycle lives. For many researchers, improving supercapacitor efficiency for multifunctional applications is a major area of study. Many elements have been employed as electrode materials to provide the best energy and power density while achieving the largest specific capacitance. Among these materials, 2D transition metal carbides and nitrides, commonly called MXenes, are emerging candidates, particularly in electrochemical energy storage applications. Because of their strength, flexibility, unique structure, increased electrical conductivity, large surface area, diversity of active sites, hydrophobicity, and hydrophilicity for cutting-edge energy storage technologies, MXenes are among the best active electrode materials. MXene, with its unique 2D layered structure, offers the infinite possibility of the intercalation of various capacitive materials. Also, MXenes have the properties of high hydrophilicity of metal oxides and high electrical conductivity of metals. Alongside, activated carbon (AC), graphene, carbon nanotubes (CNTs), transition metal oxides, and conducting polymers (CPs) act as excellent electrode materials owing to their outstanding thermal, mechanical, electrical, and morphological properties. According to recent studies, one of the perfect methods for energy storage applications is to integrate MXenes with other superior elements for generating MXene-based composite electrode materials. This review includes recent developments in the investigation of MXene-based hybrid composites for supercapacitors. It covers composite s synthesis strategies, electrode architecture, electrochemical performance, and their efficiency in supercapacitors.
conclusion: 8 Conclusion This review examines supercapacitors in detail, including their specifications, applications, development of electrode materials, and principles of operation. It was briefly mentioned how supercapacitors are categorized based on their mechanisms. The review centers on the most recent advancements in MXenes and supercapacitor research. MXenes of various kinds are synthesized and their combinations are investigated. The most thoroughly studied material is Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene, and research is currently underway. Several synthesis techniques used during the MAX phase are briefly reviewed in the current review. There are many different etching procedures available for creating MXenes, including F-free, fluoride-based, and HF acid etching. It is crucial to remember that the range of unique morphologies and adjustable surfaces could be primarily attributed to the etching circumstances. It was discovered that combining MXenes with other materials, like carbon, polymers, transition metal oxides, and MOF, for the supercapacitor electrode material improved both the electrochemical and overall mechanical performance. Non-etheless, it is frequently noted that MXene transition metal oxide composites have poor mechanical characteristics. As a result, we hope that our analysis will help researchers identify suitable MXene and activated carbon composite energy storage systems to help them overcome obstacles. Furthermore, the summary offered in this review will help future investigators to carry out their research on MXene dispersal and denudation techniques in order to produce MXene hybrids with enhanced electrochemical performance.

title: Enhanced charge storage using in-situ grown NiGa-layered double hydroxide on V4C3Tx MXene for supercapacitor applications
authors: Dana Susan Abraham, Mari Vinoba, Margandan Bhagiyalakshmi
abstract: Developing remarkable hierarchical heterostructures in nanocomposites is crucial for enhancing electrochemical performance. Heterostructures combining layered double hydroxides (LDHs) and MXenes garner considerable attention as key candidates in energy conversion and storage. By fusing conductive 2D MXenes with LDHs, the advantages of both materials are effectively harnessed. Herein, nickel gallium layered double hydroxide (NiGa-LDH) is in situ grown on the V4C3Tx MXene surface to form NiGa-LDH V4C3Tx MXene (NGV) nanocomposite. The robust interfacial interaction and superior electronic connection between NiGa-LDH and V4C3Tx MXene nanosheet bolster structural stability, enhances electrolyte accessibility, and boost electrical conductivity, thus delivers a specific capacity of 268.85 mAh g 1 for NGV-11 at 1 A g 1. The fabricated NGV-11 AC device achieves an impressive energy density of 56.41 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 800 W kg 1 and exceptional cycling stability of 93.24 retention after 5000 cycles. The results show that the synergistic interaction between NiGa-LDH and V4C3Tx MXene significantly improves the charge storage capacity in the nanocomposite. This study presents a simple and effective approach for designing vanadium-based MXene with LDH for high-performance supercapacitors.
conclusion: In summary, NiGa-LDH was in situ grown on the surface of delaminated V4 C3 Tx MXene nanosheets via a facile hydrothermal procedure leveraging the electrostatic interactions between LDH and MXene. Various ratios of nickel and gallium were explored to optimize capacity performance, resulting in the Ni-Ga (1:1) LDH V4 C3 Tx MXene (NGV-11) nanocomposite demonstrating a notable increase in specific capacity to 268.85 mAh g 1 at 1 A g 1 . This enhanced capacity can be attributed to the synergistic interaction between NiGa-LDH and V4 C3 Tx MXene, where the abundant active sites of NiGa-LDH are complemented by the superior electrical conductivity and structural stability of V4 C3 Tx MXene. NGV-11 AC supercapacitor device attained a remarkable energy density of 56.41 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 800 W kg 1 , an impressive cycling stability with 93.24 capacitance retention, and a coulombic efficiency of 96.96 after 5000 cycles. Thus, the integration of NiGa-LDH with V4 C3 Tx MXene addresses common challenges in LDH-based materials, such as low conductivity and limited cycling stability, positioning the NGV-11 nanocomposite as a competitive candidate for next-generation energy storage systems. Hence, the study shows that NiGa-LDH V4 C3 Tx MXene nanocomposite confers notable prospects as electrode material in the field of energy storage applications. Moreover, this study lays a strong foundation for advancing vanadium-based MXene-LDH hybrids in future energy storage research. title: High-performance asymmetric supercapacitors based on 2D MXene NiCoP hybrid and ZIF derived porous nanocarbon
authors: Erdenebayar Baasanjav, K.A. Sree Raj, Hafis Hakkeem, Chandra Sekhar Rout, Sang Mun Jeong
abstract: The performance of supercapacitors can be improved by strategically designing 2D MXene-based electrodes with excellent electrochemical properties. However, several challenges remain in developing hybrid materials based on 2D MXenes due to restacking, which hinders energy storage performance. In this work, we successfully synthesized a 2D MXene Ni-Co phosphide (MX NCP) hybrid material for supercapacitors via a facile hydrothermal reaction followed by phosphorization. The optimized MX NCP positive electrode showed good energy storage performance with a specific capacitance of 1754.0 F g 1 at 3 mA cm 2 in a three-electrode configuration. The synergistic effect of MXene and Ni-Co phosphide has contributed towards the enhanced charge storage performance. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) fabricated with MX NCP and porous nanocarbon (PNC) delivered a maximum energy density of 54.3 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 565.6 W kg 1 with a cycling stability of 93.8 after 10,000 cycles. To evaluate the practical versatility of the ASC, a planar device was successfully fabricated making MX NCP a promising electrode material in next-generation wearable and flexible supercapacitors.
conclusion: In summary, a 2D MXene-based NiCoP hybrid structure was successfully synthesized via a cost-effective hydrothermal reaction and phosphorization process. The designed and well-developed 2D MXene NCP composite exhibits large porous active sites, abundant redox-active sites and exceptional electrical conductivity, which collectively promote enhanced Faradaic redox reactions, efficient electrolyte diffusion, and fast electron transport. The synergistic interaction between the MXene sheets and NCP nanorods leads to remarkable electrochemical performance, achieving a high specific capacitance of 1754.0 F g 1 at 3 mA cm 2 , along with good rate capability and higher stability, with minimal loss in activity after 5000 charge discharge cycles. Additionally, a hybrid ASC device constructed using MX-3 NCP as the positive electrode and PNC as the negative electrode, delivered a high specific energy of 54.3 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 565.6 W kg 1 and maintained 32.6 Wh kg 1 at a high-power density of 6270 W kg 1 . The device also demonstrated exceptional cyclic stability by retaining 93.8 of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles and excellent adaptability in practical applications. Moreover, TMP MXene composites can be promising electrodes for the development of hybrid supercapacitor technologies. title: Synergistically coupling of ternary hydrotalcite and Ti3C2Tx-MXene nanosheets boosting electronic transmission in energy storage
authors: Lu Luo, Qiuyan Kong, Qianqian Zhang, Jing Zhang, Mizi Fan, Weigang Zhao
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDH) and two-dimensional metal carbides (Ti3C2Tx) garner significant attention in recent years. LDH Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids combine the unique characteristics of individual component, making them a promising option for high-power energy storage applications. Here, we present a composite electrode constructed by synergistic coupling of Ti3C2Tx and ternary hydrotalcite (NiCoMn-LDH). Strong interfacial interactions between the NiCoMn-LDH array and Ti3C2Tx nanoflakes, along with effective electron coupling, contribute to enhanced structural stability, conductivity, and electrolyte accessibility, thereby significantly promoting the kinetics of redox reactions. The intriguing lace-like structure fully utilizes the high activity of NiCoMn-LDH and the excellent conductivity of Ti3C2Tx, allowing LDH Ti3C2Tx to exhibit an impressive output capacitance of 1102.9 F g 1 at 1 A g 1, coupled with notable rate capability (66.87 at 20 A g 1). The constructed LDH Ti3C2Tx AC hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) achieves a remarkable energy density of 47.3 Wh kg 1 at 800 W kg 1. Following 5000 cycles, the specific capacity of HSC decreases by merely 8.3 , while achieving a Coulombic efficiency of 99 , showcasing remarkable durability and reversible reaction characteristics. This study provides a streamlined and effective methodology for crafting LDH Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids, showcasing robust coupled interfaces and exceptional electrochemical energy storage application.
conclusion: 4 Conclusions In summary, the LDH Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrids with intriguing lace-like structure were successfully developed via synergistically coupling Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with ternary hydrotalcite (NiCoMn-LDH). The disordered crisscross arrangement of the NiCoMn-LDH arrays have enabled a high porosity and abundant active sites. Coupled with Ti 3 C 2 T x serving as an electronic transmission bridge, the LDH Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrid exhibits outstanding electrical conductivity, showcasing a remarkable specific capacitance of 1102.9 F g 1 and demonstrating a rate capability of 66.87 at 20 A g 1 . Further assembly of the LDH Ti 3 C 2 T x -2 AC hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) yields a maximum energy density of 47.3 Wh kg 1 (at 800 W kg 1 ), maintaining a considerable energy density of 35.7 Wh kg 1 even at 8000 W kg 1 . Moreover, the HSC device demonstrates distinguished durability (91.7 ) and Coulombic efficiency (99 ) after 5000 cycles. This work highlights the rational combination of 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x with highly active transition metal compounds, showcasing their synergistic effects in enhancing the performance of nanohybrids. This presents thrilling possibilities for the design of devices for electrochemical energy harvesting and storage.

title: Nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) pillared Ta4C3Tx MXene as high-performance electrochemical supercapacitors
authors: Sabeen Fatima, M. Waqas Hakim, Xiaoxiao Zheng, Yu Sun, Ziheng Li, Nan Han, Muyang Li, Zeyuan Wang, Lei Han, Liang Wang, Safia Khan, Jiangwei Liu, Hu Li
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials are proved to possess outstanding energy storage capabilities for advanced supercapacitors, yet these materials require modification to overcome field obstacles and reach their full potential. Here, we prepared tantalum carbide MXene and nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) by adopting facile synthesis routes. Surface engineering of 2D tantalum carbide sheets is carefully performed with zero-dimensional graphene to achieve NGQD Ta4C3Tx nanosheets. The compositional analysis demonstrated the attachment of quantum dots with MXene sheets. The modified 1.5 -NGQD Ta4C3Tx, 3 -NGQD Ta4C3Tx, 5 -NGQD Ta4C3Tx, 7 -NGQD Ta4C3Tx and 10 -NGQD Ta4C3Tx nanosheets presented enhanced energy storage capability than NGQD and plain MXene. Graphene quantum dots enable Ta4C3Tx to have faster more stable reaction kinetics and enhance the gravimetric capacitance 7 folds (701 F g) compared to plain MXene (100 F g). Due to the exceptional working electrode performances, an asymmetric supercapacitor is also fabricated with NGQD Ta4C3Tx nanosheets as working electrode. The device exhibited a pseudocapacitive battery-like storage mechanism with a specific capacity of 110 Cg-1, power and energy densities of 9000 W kg and 55 W-h Kg respectively. Due to the low corrosion rate exhibited by Tafel plots an excellent capacity retention is observed up to 20000 cycles. The study imparts valuable insights into engineering 0D 2D nanostructures for next-generation energy storage systems.
conclusion: In this study, we have prepared Ta4 C3 Tx MXene and nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) using easy and cost-effective synthesis routes. Ta4 C3 Tx MXene sheets were surface engineered via NGQD by adopting a solvothermal synthesis approach. Various NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were created by carefully regulating the surface engineering of Ta4 C3 Tx sheets with NGQD varying concentrations from 1.5 to 10 . For the assessment of working materials quality, shape, crystallinity, chemical structure, and elemental content, different supporting characterizations such as UV vis, PL, Raman, XRD, TEM, FTIR, SEM and XPS were also performed. The effective synthesis and excellent quality of every material were explained by these characterizations. To test the charge storage capabilities NGQD, Ta4 C3 Tx , 1.5 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx , 3 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx , 5 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx , 7 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx, and 10 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were employed as working electrodes in 1 M KOH electrolyte. With the attachment of nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots the charge storage of Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets was not only enhanced up to sevenfold but also displayed excellent stability for 20k repeated cycles. The performance evaluation of 5 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx AC capacitor device demonstrated charge storage characteristics in between pseudocapacitance and battery-like properties, along with long-term stability. Also, the increased specific capacity, power, and energy density of the device make 5 -NGQD Ta4 C3 Tx a superior candidate for energy storage device applications. All things considered, this work offers guidance on how to modify dense MXene phases, such as tantalum carbide, to improve their electrochemical device performances relative to their plain forms. title: Improving the bimetallic interactions of CeO2 MnO2 MXenes for supercapacitor electrode applications
authors: Faiz Imran, Azmat Hussain, Ibrahim Aladhyani, Fawad Ali, Shahbaz Afzal, Raphael M. Obodo
abstract: The characteristics of large surface area, high chemical firmness and virtuous electrical conductivity make MXene-based electrodes an emerging potential material for supercapacitor electrode applications. The qualities of invented electrodes were examined using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), UV visible spectroscopy, and electrochemical analysis. The estimated specific capacitance of 1370 F g-1 from cyclic voltammetry (CV) at a scan rate of 1.0 mVs 1 and 1520 F g-1 from galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) at 0.5 Ag-1 current density, respectively, were obtained from the CeO2 MnO2 MXene electrode. The study s findings suggest that the addition of MXene caused the manufactured electrodes electrochemical properties to improve. The electrodes CeO2 MXene, MnO2 MXene, and CeO2 MnO2 MXene have proven to be quite effective, which makes them a good option for supercapacitor electrode application. The CeO2 MnO2 MXene electrode was found to exhibit remarkable cyclic stability at 0.5 Ag-1 current density, maintaining 73.5 of its initial measurements after 10,000 full cycles.
conclusion: Summarily, CeO2 MXene, MnO2 MXene, and CeO2 MnO2 MXene nanocomposites have been effectively produced utilizing the SILAR deposition process. Nanocrystals with sizes ranging from 32.68 to 38.55 nm were evenly attached to the MXene sheets, making them suitable for use as electrode materials in supercapacitors. The results indicate that the composite electrode exhibited impressive specific capacitance values of 1123, 1270, 1520, and 873, 1020, 1265 F g-1 , respectively, when subjected to GCD tests at current densities of 0.5 Ag-1 and 1.0 Ag-1 . In addition, when these electrodes were used to interact with the CV at a scan rate of 1.0 mVs 1 , they exhibited specific capacitances of 972, 1125, and 1370 F g-1 , respectively. The CeO2 MnO2 MXene electrode demonstrated the highest specific capacitance, energy, and power densities. Remarkably, it maintained 73.4 of its capacity after undergoing 10,000 full cycles. These electrodes exhibited high specific capacitance due to two charge storage mechanisms: electric double-layer capacitance from the Mene and pseudo capacitance from CeO2 and MnO2 , respectively. This can be attributed to an increase in the types and quantity of ions, as well as the presence of MXene, which promotes the formation of stronger connections between different ions and improves the structure and shape of nanoparticles. title: A one-pot strategy for modifying the surface of Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Ken Aldren S. Usman, Mia Judicpa, Christine Jurene O. Bacal, Kevinilo P. Marquez, Jizhen Zhang, Bhagya Dharmasiri, James D. Randall, Luke C. Henderson, Joselito M. Razal
abstract: Surface modification of MXenes significantly expands their potential for a wide range of applications. Here, we demonstrate a one-pot spontaneous polymerization of acrylic acid onto MXene sheet surfaces using an aryl diazonium coupling agent (nitrobenzene diazonium salt) as an approach to tune MXene interfacial properties. We use this formation of polymer coatings as a coagulation strategy for spinning fibers from liquid crystal MXene dispersions, obtaining densified free-standing fibers with tensile strength and breaking energy of 155 MPa and 4.5 MJ m 3. This simple method potentially offers a scalable approach for fabricating functional MXene macroarchitectures.
conclusion: We demonstrated a one-pot polymerization of acrylate monomers, facilitated by the spontaneous reaction of MXene with aryl diazonium species. Unlike most surface radical-initiated methods, we successfully tuned the MXene surface while achieving minimal damage to its inherent chemical composition. This polymerization strategy enabled the coagulation of extruded LC-MXene dispersions into strong and delamination-resistant fibers. The method allows for simultaneous MXene densification and surface functionalization and provides an efficient method for fabricating MXene-based macro-architectures with tailored interfacial properties. title: Cylindrical janus Mosse CNT intercalated into Mxene: A high-performance supercapacitor electrode with high volumetric capacity and flexibility
authors: Nouf Alharbi
abstract: Restoring MXene s intrinsic capacitive function is essential for high-performance supercapacitors. This study presents a new approach to tackle the problem of restacking and improving energy storage. It involves incorporating MoSSe CNT (MoSSe nanosheets wrapped around carbon nanotubes) into MXene films, which are exceptionally electrochemically active. After optimisation, the MoSSe CNT MXene electrode demonstrates remarkable volumetric and gravimetric capacitance values of 1819 F cm ³ and 585 F g ¹, respectively. The exceptional performance of MoSSe CNT arises from the combined effects of MoSSe CNT acting as both spacers and active contributors to pseudocapacitance. The electrode obtained exhibits exceptional rate capability, flexibility, and a high energy density of 47.5 Wh L ¹, making it a highly promising contender for advanced energy storage systems.
conclusion: To summarize, this study introduces a new and efficient approach for producing high-performance supercapacitor electrodes by integrating MoSSe CNT into MXene sheets. The MoSSe CNT hybrids function as effective spacers to inhibit the restacking of MXene while also making a major contribution to the overall pseudocapacitance. The MoSSe CNT MXene electrode has outstanding volumetric energy storage capacity (1819 F cm 3 ), impressive rate capability, and extraordinary adaptability. In addition, the artificially created symmetrical supercapacitor exhibits a remarkable energy density, emphasizing the potential of this method in the advancement of flexible and high-performance energy storage devices for supplying power to small and portable electronic gadgets. title: Self-assembled MXene(Ti3C2Tx) α-Fe2O3 nanocomposite as negative electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Ren Zou, Hongying Quan, Menghua Pan, Shuai Zhou, Dezhi Chen, Xubiao Luo
abstract: To further improve the electrochemical performance of MXene materials, MXene(Ti3C2Tx) α-Fe2O3 nanocomposites are fabricated by a self-assembly method via electrostatic attraction between negatively charged Ti3C2Tx MXenesand positively charged cocoa-like α-Fe2O3 nanoparticles at room temperature. As a negative electrode material, the resulting nanocomposites show excellent electrochemical performance, including a wide operating potential of 1.2 V ( 1.2 0 V), a high specific capacitance of 405.4 F g 1 at the current density of 2 A g 1 and a specific capacitance of 197.6 F g 1 even at the current density of 20 A g 1 in 5 M LiCl. In addition, the nanocomposites possess a high cycling stability with 97.7 capacitance retention of the initial capacitance after 2000 cycles. The impressive results indicate that the prepared MXene(Ti3C2Tx) α-Fe2O3 nanocomposites is a promising negative electrode material for supercapacitor. The self-assemble of MXenes and metal oxides will provide more opportunities for their application in energy storage.
conclusion: MXene α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites were prepared through electrostatic attraction with the aid of surfactant. The prepared nanostructure could effective inhibit the restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and facilitate electrolyte transport of α-Fe2 O3. Owing to the high conductivity of Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and the high specific capacitance of α-Fe2 O3 , the fabricated MXene α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites exhibited a high specific capacitance up to 405.4 F g 1 at the current density of 2 A g 1 , and still 197.62 F g 1 (48.9 remaining) at the current density of 20 A g 1 . In addition, the MXene α-Fe2 O3 electrode showed high cycling stability with 97.7 retention of the initial capacitance after 2000 cycles at a scan rate of 100 mV s 1 . The excellent electrochemical performance of the MXene α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites demonstrates their potential as negative electrode materials for supercapacitors, and our work provides some new thoughts for the synthesis of MXene metal oxides nanocomposites. title: A capacitance-enhanced MXene anode for high-performance and dual-functional quasi-solid-state ammonium ion hybrid supercapacitor
authors: Qiang Wang, Shenshen Guan, Ranyun Wu, Liangliang Su, Yalong Yang, Xulai Zhu, Yuxia Hu, Junpeng Zhang, Jia Si, Wei Zeng
abstract: The aqueous ammonium ion hybrid supercapacitor (AIHSC) for dual-energy storage mechanisms of bulk intercalation and bulk adsorption has attracted extensive attention from researchers in the field of energy storage. However, AIHSC currently lacks sufficiently effective anode materials with high capacitance and stability. Pre-intercalated MXene electrodes have demonstrated high-capacity advantages in the fields of magnesium and zinc ion energy storage, but there have been no research reports in the field of AIHSC. Here, for the first time, pre-intercalated MXene was used as the anode material for AIHSC, and a high-performance multifunctional AIHSC was constructed by combining it with multi-walled carbon nanotubes-FeFe(CN)6 cathode. A series of characterizations and theoretical calculations show that pre-intercalated strategies can effectively enhance the electrochemical properties of MXene. As a result, the pre-intercalated MXene anode shows a superior ammonium storage capacitance of 252 F g 1 and a high stability of 6000 cycles. The quasi-solid-state AIHSC also displays the excellent electrochemical performance and can be directly used as a pressure sensor to monitor external pressure changes and human limb movements. This study provides a viable path to the effective development of high-performance multifunctional AIHSCs and their anodes.
conclusion: the characterization section confirms the successful preparation of MXene-CTAB and MWCNT-FeHCF electrode materials. The electrochemical test results of anodes show that the MXene-CTAB electrode has a higher specific capacitance of 252 F g 1 compared to that of MXene electrode (197 F g 1 ). The theoretical calculations show the intercalation of CTA+ ions facilitates the transfer of electrons and ions, enhances the adsorption and binding ability of NH4 + to MXene, and reduces the diffusion barrier of NH4 + . The electrochemical test results of cathodes show that the MWCNT-FeHCF electrode also has superior electrochemical performance. The QSS AIHSC constructed based on the MXene-CTAB anode, the (NH4)2 SO4 -PAMH electrolyte and the MWCNT-FeHCF cathode shows superior electrochemical properties, such as a high specific capacitance (122 F g 1 ), high energy density (43 Wh kg 1 ), high power density (800 W kg 1 ) and high cycling stability (capacitance retention is 83 after 2000 cycles). In addition, the QSS AIHSC demonstrates a wide pressure monitoring interval (1 11 N) and high responsiveness (210 ms) when applied as a pressure sensor, and it is able to differentiate finger joint movements through pressure detection. Therefore, MXene-CTAB is an excellent anode material, and the multifunctional QSS AIHSC constructed on the basis of MXene-CTAB anode has a broad application value. title: Capacitance performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets on alkaline and neutral electrolytes
authors: Ramesh Aravind Murugesan, Krishna Chandar Nagamuthu Raja
abstract: The high electrical conductivity, good hydrophilicity, and various surface terminal configurations of MXenes have exposed extensive attention in the field of energy storage. Ti3C2Tx MXene was synthesised via a facile chemical process. A study of Ti3C2Tx MXene s structure, composition, and morphology was carried out using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy (RS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). A detailed study of the influence of aqueous electrolytes on the charge storage performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene was conducted by cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD), cyclic stability (CS), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). In addition, it is proposed that Ti3C2Tx MXene s surface terminations affect its capacitance behaviour in aqueous electrolytes. Ti3C2Tx MXene in 3 M (KOH) alkaline electrolyte has good electrochemical performance, with a specific capacitance (Cs) of up to 92 F g at 2A g, making it a potential material for supercapacitors.
conclusion: A facile HF etching wet chemical method was used to synthesize the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene assembled with many expandable nanosheets. An extremely significant effect of aqueous electrolyte composition on capacitance behaviour is revealed in the present study of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrodes. In terms of specific capacitance, we obtained maximum values of 92 F g 1 in KOH and 75 F g 1 in Na2 SO4 electrolytes at 2 A g. However, the 3 M KOH of Ti3 C2 TX MXene has a highly stable capacitance retention rate of 73 compared with a 51 retention rate for 3 M Na2 SO4 of Ti3 C2 TX MXene after 10,000 cycles. Due to its high conductivity and pseudocapacitive, the 3 M KOH alkaline electrolyte of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene shows excellent electrochemical capacitor application than the 3 M Na2 SO4 neutral electrolyte. title: Unveiling the potential: Asymmetric supercapacitors with conductive polymers Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4 electrodes deliver high energy densities
authors: Xuguang Wang, Kai Song, Hongtao Yang, Ruxangul Jamal, Tursun Abdiryim, Abdukeyum Abdurexit, Nana Fan, Yajun Liu, Jiabei Li, Jiachang Liu
abstract: Ti3C2Tx is considered a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its fast electronic properties, excellent hydrophilicity and mechanical properties. However, severe Ti3C2Tx nanosheet stacking reduces the exposed active sites and hinders the ion diffusion of Ti3C2Tx, leading to poor electrochemical performance. Here, we report a strategy for doping of Ti3C2Tx, in which the Ni3S4 and conducting polymer (CP) were selected as doping agent for Ti3C2Tx, and it is expected that metal sulfide and CP can overcome the defects of Ti3C2Tx. In this work, the conducting polymers were as polyaniline (PANI), polypyrrole (PPY) and poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT). As a result, the prepared composites exhibit superior multiplicative capacity with a capacitance of 2502 F g-1 (PANI Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4), 2440 F g-1 (PPY Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4), and 2620 F g-1 (PEDOT Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4), respectively. In addition, CP Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4 AC asymmetric supercapacitors were assembled with energy densities of 60.2 (PANI Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4), 86.7 (PPY Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4), and 53.4 (PEDOT Ti3C2Tx Ni3S4) Wh kg-1 at 1,500 W kg-1, respectively. This work develops a simple way to prepare the porous Ti3C2Tx film for supercapacitors with excellent electrochemical performance.
conclusion: In summary, we propose a new strategy for doping Ni3S4 and conducting polymers on Ti3 C2 Tx . Ni3 S4 as an intercalator increases the layer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx . Meanwhile, the hydrogen bonding interactions between the conducting polymer and Ti3 C2 Tx break the electrostatic equilibrium of the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, leading to the assembly of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets into a three-dimensional porous structure. As a result, the composites have excellent rate properties, the mass specific capacity is significantly enhanced and reaches 2502 F g-1 (PANI Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 ), 2440 F g-1 (PPY Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 ), and 2620 F g-1 (PEDOT Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 ), respectively. In addition, CP Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC asymmetric supercapacitors were assembled with energy densities of 60.2 (PANI Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC), 86.7 (PPY Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC), and 53.4 (PEDOT Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC) Wh kg-1 at 1500 W kg-1 , respectively. Notably, the supercapacitor exhibits excellent cycling capability with 93.42 (PANI Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC), 93.28 (PPY Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC) and 96.16 (PEDOT Ti3 C2 Tx Ni3 S4 AC) capacitance retention after 20,000 cycles. The present work opens a new way to prepare porous Ti3C2Tx composites with excellent electrochemical properties. title: A Ti3C2Tx-encapsulated Mn2+-doped Co(OH)2 nanosheets electrode grown on carbon cloth for low-temperature flexible supercapacitors
authors: Wenfeng Zhang, Yan Shan, Xuegang Yu, Kezheng Chen
abstract: In general, most flexible supercapacitors with excellent performance at room temperature cannot work properly at relatively low temperatures (such as 0 C), mainly due to the poor cold resistance of the electrodes and electrolytes. In this paper, the carbon cloth was coated with positively charged Mn2+-doped Co(OH)2 coating by electrodeposition and then impregnated with negatively charged Ti3C2Tx nanosheets suspension (This electrode is named CC Co(OH)2:Mn2+ Tx, Where x is the number of impregnation Ti3C2Tx.). The results show that the obtained electrode has a good supercapacitor performance with the specific capacitance of 22.13 F g 1 (the area specific capacitance of the sample is 202.5 mF cm 2), which is attributed to the synergistic effect of Ti3C2Tx and the flower microstructure of Mn2+-doped Co(OH)2 coating. Ti3C2Tx was introduced to polyvinyl alcohol sodium alginate hydrogel electrolyte to obtain a new antifreezing organohydrogel and then a flexible asymmetric supercapacitor was assembled with CC Co(OH)2:Mn2+ T3 as the positive electrode, CC T3 as negative electrode, and the performance of the supercapacitor at 25 C and at 0 C were investigated. It was found the supercapacitor exhibited better performance at 0 C instead of 25 C. When the current density is 5 mA cm 2, the area specific capacitance of the supercapacitor at 0 C reaches 52.02 mF cm 2. After 1000 cycles, the supercapacitor has a capacitance retention rate of 82.5 at 0 C, which is much higher than that of 55.15 at 25 C. The reason may be related to the Ti3C2Tx and the crosslinked networks structures of composite hydrogel. The results show that the supercapacitor has excellent working ability at 0 C, which provides the possibility for the device to work normally in low temperature.
conclusion: In summary, we have successfully prepared an unbonded CC Co(OH)2 :Mn2+ T3 flexible electrode, which is assembled by the electrostatic interaction between the positive charge coating deposited on the surface of carbon cloth and the electronegative Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets. The electrodeposited Mn2+ -doped Co(OH)2 coating has a larger specific surface area and more active sites, which helps to improve the specific capacitance of the electrode. The mass specific capacitance of the best electrode reached 22.13 F g 1 . The electrode still has a Coulomb efficiency of 92.8 after 1000 charge and discharge cycles, demonstrating good cycle stability. Moreover, the flexible electrode is used as a positive electrode to assemble a supercapacitor with LiCl as electrolyte. The area specific capacitance of the device reaches 52.02 mF cm 2 at 0 C, much higher than that at 25 C (2.36 mF cm 2 ). Meanwhile, the supercapacitor still has a capacitance retention rate of 82.5 after 1000 cycles at 0 C, indicating the supercapacitor is suitable for operation at 0 C. The flexible electrodes and FSCs prepared in this study are expected to be applied in the fields of wearable devices, flexible sensor power supply and portable electronic devices. title: Construct interface pollared lared interaction in Co-MOF MXene as high flexibility electrode for solid-state hybrid supercapacitor
authors: Bingzhe Jia, Xinrui Qiang, Lei Wang, Jiale Wang, Haibo Che, Jiarui Li, YiChi Liu, Zhiqiang Li, Yufei Wang, Xiaodie Huang, Xinming Wu
abstract: Energy storage devices based on MXene flexible electrodes have advantages such as high electrochemical performance, but their flexible cycling stability limits their further commercial applications. Based on this, this work presents a high-performance Co(terephthalic acid, triethylenediamine) Ti3C2 MXene (Co(BDC, TEDA) Ti3C2) hybrid electrode fabricated through in situ growth of three-dimensional Co(BDC, TEDA) MOFs within Ti3C2 MXene interlayers via a one-step solvothermal approach. The rationally designed heterostructure achieves synergistic performance enhancement through three key interface engineering effects: interlayer expansion, complementary conductivity-redox, and covalent interface bonding. Electrochemical characterization demonstrates outstanding performance metrics, including a specific capacitance of 214.65 F g 1 at 100 mA g 1, an energy density of 10.73 Wh kg 1, and remarkable cycling stability with 93.1 capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles, significantly outperforming individual components. First-principles calculations reveal a 129 enhancement in Na adsorption energy ( 2.18 eV vs. 0.95 eV for pristine MXene), providing atomic-level insights into the improved energy storage mechanisms. Furthermore, asymmetric flexible devices show excellent mechanical flexibility and can withstand bending at 0 90 while keeping electrochemical performance constant. This work offers a promising strategy for designing flexible, high-performance electrodes with strong potential for practical applications.
conclusion: This study demonstrates the successful development of a high-performance Co(BDC, TEDA) Ti₃C₂ hybrid electrode material achieved through strategic interface engineering. By combining conductive Ti3 C2 MXene with redox-active Co(BDC, TEDA) MOF via a one-step solvothermal method, we have created a composite that effectively overcomes the limitations of both components through synergistic integration. Comprehensive experimental characterization and DFT calculations reveal three key enhancement mechanisms: (1) covalent Ti O Co interfacial bonds that facilitate efficient charge transfer, (2) expanded interlayer spacing (9.13 10.9 Å) that promotes ion diffusion, and (3) a 129 improvement in Na adsorption energy ( 2.18 vs 0.95 eV). These structural advantages translate to exceptional electrochemical performance, including a high specific capacitance of 214.65 F g ¹ at 100 mA g ¹ and excellent cycling stability with 93.1 retention after 10,000 cycles at 500 mA g 1 significantly surpassing both the individual components and comparable hybrid systems. Importantly, the flexible device based on this material demonstrates excellent mechanical adaptability, maintaining stable electrochemical performance under repeated bending from 0 to 90 , highlighting its suitability for wearable energy storage applications. This work provides a practical design strategy for MXene MOF hybrid electrodes and offers valuable insights into the development of flexible energy storage materials with balanced electrochemical performance and mechanical adaptability. The demonstrated interface engineering approach can be further extended to other material systems for diverse electrochemical applications, while future work should focus on component optimization and scalable fabrication strategies for practical deployment. title: MXene tungsten-functionalized graphene oxide nanosheets as conductive platforms for FeNi-Co-doped MnO2 Nanocomposites: Toward high-performance supercapacitor electrodes
authors: N.D. Raskar, D.V. Dake, V.A. Mane, R.B. Sonpir, V.D. Mote, M. Vasundhara, P.C. Zine, M.D. Shirsat, K.P. Gattu, B.N. Dole
abstract: The present manuscript has synthesized the innovative nanocomposite of tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide (TGO) based FeNi codoped MnO2 (TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2) which has better supercapacitor performance than the tungsten carbide (TC) MXene-based nanocomposite sample (TC-3 FeNi-MnO2). The first motive of the manuscript is to manufacture lower-cost materials with better properties with higher stability. Nowadays, worldwide researchers are focusing on MXene materials and reporting the best smart material for multiple applications but the present manuscript has done an innovative study and found that the graphene-based materials have good properties with higher stability like MXene samples. The prepared nanocomposite samples have been characterized by XRD, FE-SEM, BET, XPS, Fluorescence spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry. X-ray diffraction (XRD) investigation demonstrated that mixed phases of tetragonal α-MnO2 and cubic α-Mn2O3 were observed. The nanocomposite of tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide-based FeNi codoped MnO2 has a nanorod-like morphology which was better than all synthesized samples. The higher capacitance found for the tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide-based Fe-Ni codoped MnO2 sample is 883 F g 1. The impact of the surface area (317.42 m2 g), defects, and structural parameters on capacitance enhancement was studied in detail. The TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2 sample has higher surface defects which was attributed by XPS and fluorescence spectroscopy.
conclusion: In conclusion, a hydrothermal approach was successfully employed to synthesize pure and FeNi-codoped MnO2 nanocomposites based on tungsten-decorated graphene oxide (TGO) and tungsten carbide (MXene). When a large radius FeNi ion is substituted for Mn ion in the octahedral position of MnO2 , defects are created and the morphologies are changed. The morphology, surface area, chemical content, and crystal structure were examined by a variety of characterization methods, including XRD, HRTEM with SAED, FE-SEM, Fluorescence, BET, and XPS. It was determined from the XRD, that TGO-based samples, such as TGO-MnO2 and TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2 , showed a mixed phase of tetragonal α-MnO2 and cubic α-Mn2 O3 . The TC-based samples, namely TC-MnO2 and TC-3 FeNi-MnO2 , exhibited an identical mixed-phase structure. The TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2 nanocomposite contains well-separated nanorods, according to the FE-SEM data. BET results show the TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2 sample shows a surface area of 317.42 m2 g which is higher than other synthesized samples. The synergistic combination of TGO composition and FeNi doping in the MnO2 lattice yielded the highest surface area, enhancing electrochemical performance. The TGO-3 FeNi-MnO2 nanocomposite demonstrated the greatest specific capacitance of 883 F g 1 , as demonstrated by its electrochemical performance. Fe and Ni doping make TGO-based MnO2 the ideal material to employ as an electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors by improving its overall performance. The functionalization of graphene oxide by making it tungsten-decorated rGO (TGO) shows superior performance than commercial Mxene (tungsten carbide) has been proved. title: Optimizing ZnSe microspheres through 2D MXene for asymmetric pseudocapacitive supercapacitors and efficient hydrogen production via water splitting
authors: Inaam Ullah, Ayesha Irfan, Mai Li, Samira Saddique, Tiantian Yang, Hanxue Zhao, Nimra Irshad, Kaishuai Yang, Chunrui Wang, Paul K. Chu
abstract: In response to the increasing demand for sustainable energy, recent efforts have focused on developing novel composites with improved crystalline structures, chemical stability, and conductivity for electrochemical applications. Self-assembled zinc selenide (ZnSe) microspheres are synthesized by a simple hydrothermal process, and their electrochemical applications as a positive electrode electrocatalyst in asymmetric pseudocapacitive supercapacitor (APSC) and water splitting are investigated. ZnSe is integrated into the two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets that serve as a physical barrier to mitigate agglomeration, prevent side reactions of Zn, provide ZnSe with more sites and a steady Zn2+ supply, ultimately enhancing the electrochemical performance. Composite electrode demonstrates superior specific capacitance of 1673.8 F g 1 at 1 A g 1, remarkable cyclic stability (98.81 capacity retention over 10,000 cycles), and excellent pseudocapacitive performance of 88 at 60 mV s 1. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations displayed highest adsorption energy for ZnSe Ti3C2Tx, showcasing stable structure and strong electron interaction. To demonstrate the commercial viability, active carbon (AC) is employed as the cathode to fabricate the AC ZnSe Ti3C2Tx-APSC device. In the water splitting assessment, ZnSe Ti3C2Tx shows the lowest Tafel slopes ( 51.3 mV dec 1 for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and 36.9 mV dec 1 for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER)). This novel approach significantly advances the overall performance of APSC and water-splitting.
conclusion: In this study, the morphological and crystallographic properties of hydrothermally synthesized ZnSe microspheres are optimized. The synergistic effects rendered by the 2D-MXene nanosheets enhance the electrochemical performance in the APSC device as well as the water-splitting setup. The ZnSe electrode shows good electrochemical performance, but self-aggregation and side reactions of Zn restrict the performance of the cathode and applications. The Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets function as a physical barrier to alleviate agglomeration and impeding side reactions of Zn, thereby enabling ZnSe to expose more sites in addition to a consistent supply of Zn2+ , ultimately augmenting the reversibility, enhancing the cyclic stability, and diminishing the overpotential. The composite electrode demonstrates superior integrity and dispersion, resulting in a longer discharging time than the ZnSe electrode. The ZnSe Ti3 C2 Tx electrode shows outstanding cyclic stability (98.81 capacity retention for 10,000 cycles), high specific capacitance of 1673.8 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 , and remarkable pseudocapacitive behavior of 88 at 60 mV s 1 . DFT results confirm the higher adsorption energy, high electron density, and stable structure of the composite electrodes. The AC ZnSe Ti3 C2 Tx -APSC device demonstrates remarkable cyclic stability, energy density, and high specific capacitance boding well for energy storage applications. LSV reveals that the ZnSe Ti3 C2 Tx electrode has a remarkable tafel slope in OER ( 51.3 mV dec 1 ) compared to ZnSe (68.7 mV dec 1 ) besides outstanding properties of ZnSe Ti3 C2 Tx in HER. This innovative approach effectively mitigates the inherent limitations of ZnSe and significantly enhances the overall electrochemical performance, positioning the ZnSe Ti3 C2 Tx as a promising candidate for energy storage and water splitting applications. title: Revealing the ionic storage mechanisms of Mo2VC2Tz (MXene) in multiple aqueous electrolytes for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Xiaodie Xuan, Yangyang Xie, Yi Tang, Jianghong Zhou, Zhao Bi, Junhui Zou, Yu-ang Lei, Jiahang Gao, Lu Li, Aibo Zhang, Chenhui Yang
abstract: It is evident that 2D MXene nanomaterials have considerable potential in the domain of electrochemical energy storage. However, the majority of extant studies concentrate on monometallic MXene, and the structural evolution and energy storage mechanisms of bimetallic solid-solution MXene (e.g. Mo2VC2Tz) remain to be elucidated. In this work, flexible, self-supported Mo2VC2Tz films have been fabricated by in situ solid-solution sintering of Mo2VAlC2 and liquid phase etching of the Al layer. The as-prepared Mo2VC2Tz features a unique bimetallic solid-solution structure with expanded interlayer spacing (15.0 Å vs. 9.2 Å in precursor), oxygen-dominated surface termination groups, and enhanced electronic conductivity (258.4 S cm 1) owing to strong Mo-V d-orbital hybridization. The electrochemical properties in hybrid supercapacitors (HSCs) were systematically evaluated in acidic (H2SO4), neutral (Na2SO4, Li2SO4, ZnSO4, Al2(SO4)3, Zn(CF3SO3)2), and alkaline (KOH) electrolytes. The results demonstrate that the Mo2VC2Tz film electrode in 1M H2SO4 exhibits superior pseudocapacitance performance, achieving a gravimetric capacitance of 257.6 F g 1 at 0.1 A g 1, which is nearly four times higher than in neutral electrolytes (e.g., 65.8 F g 1 in 1M Li2SO4). Furthermore, the Mo2VC2Tz exhibited exceptional cycling stability in 1M H2SO4, retaining 95.71 of its initial capacity after 20,000 cycles. Density functional theory calculations revealed the evolution of the electron state distribution before and after V doping in Mo2VC2Tz. Additionally, the interfacial interaction mechanisms between V atoms and cations (H+, Li+, Na+, Zn2+, Al3+ and K+) were elucidated. Therefore, this study provides a theoretical basis for the design of bimetallic MXene in various electrolyte systems, and promotes the development of high-performance HSCs.
conclusion: To sum up, 2D few-layer bimetallic Mo2 VC2 Tz MXene nanomaterials have been successfully prepared by introducing high electrochemical activity V atoms into the precursor MAX. The unique bimetallic solid-solution structure of Mo2 VC2 Tz has an enlarged layer spacing and oxygen-dominated surface termini, which together enhance ion accessibility and redox active site density. The electrochemical results indicate that at a current density of 0.1 A g 1 , the Mo2 VC2 Tz electrodes in 1M H2 SO4 , 1M Al2 (SO4 )3 , and 1M KOH have a top three high specific capacitances in 257.6, 143.4, and 134.4 F g 1 , respectively. In an acidic electrolyte, the oxidation-reduction reaction is effectively promoted by the strong interaction between hydrated hydrogen ions (protons) and oxygen-containing functional groups on the surface of the electrode materials, so that the specific capacitance of the system is significantly higher than that of other electrolytic liquid systems. After 20,000 cycles, the Mo2 VC2 Tz film electrode retains a capacity retention rate of 95.71 in the 1M H2 SO4 electrolyte and the Coulomb efficiency is close to 100 . Confirmed by DFT calculations showing increased density of states near the Fermi level and reduced H+ adsorption energy. These structural and electronic modifications synergistically promote rapid proton diffusion and reversible multivalent redox reactions, establishing Mo2 VC2 Tz as a high-performance electrode material for acidic electrolyte-based supercapacitors. In general, this study not only provides theoretical guidance for the application of bimetallic solid-solution MXene materials in the field of energy storage, but also establish an innovative research foundation for the development of high-performance electrochemical energy storage devices by combining experiment and theory. title: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) anodes for asymmetric supercapacitors with high active mass loading
authors: Xuelin Li, Jianfeng Zhu, Wenyu Liang, Igor Zhitomirsky
abstract: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) is an emerging material choice for advanced energy storage. However, the relatively low areal capacitance is a bottleneck in developing asymmetric supercapacitors with enhanced energy-power characteristics in large voltage windows. A simple and straightforward approach is proposed to design and fabricate Ti3C2Tx-multiwalled carbon nanotube (Ti3C2Tx-CNT) composite electrodes. Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) is used as a binder for electrodes with 40 mg cm 2 high active mass loadings (AML); meanwhile, both multilayered Ti3C2Tx and CNT are efficiently dispersed in PMMA solution. The fabricated Ti3C2Tx-CNT electrodes with different CNT contents are tested in a 1.1 -0.3 V negative potential window and analyzed by different electrochemical techniques. The optimization of Ti3C2Tx-CNT-PMMA composition facilitates the design of anodes with capacitance of 2.26 F cm 2 in Na2SO4 electrolyte, which is essentially higher than literature results for Ti3C2Tx. The ability to obtain high capacitance in the Na2SO4 electrolyte is a crucial result, which facilitates the fabrication of asymmetric aqueous devices operating at 1.6 V. The Ti3C2Tx-CNT anode is combined with a MnO2-CNT cathode in an asymmetric cell, which shows a 1.24 F cm 2 capacitance at 3 mA cm 2.
conclusion: We developed a high-performance Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT composite electrode containing 20 CNT with a 40 mg cm 2 high AML, which can deliver excellent rate performance, a 2.26 F cm 2 high areal capacitance, and long-term cyclic stability in a negative potential range. The enhanced capacitive behavior benefits from the synergy between Ti3 C2 Tx layers and a proper amount of CNT to form more interconnected nanopores for efficient electrolyte ions transfer, improved electronic conductivity, and build more accessible nanostructure for effective reactions. The high mass loadings benefit from an advanced PMMA binder, in which solution multilayered Ti3 C2 Tx and multiwalled carbon nanotube can be well dispersed and mixed. A MnO2 -CNT composite electrode with a 20 carbon nanotube was also fabricated by the same procedure and tested in a positive potential window. Asymmetric devices operating in a cell voltage of 1.6 V consisted of Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT-20 anodes and MnO2 -CNT-20 cathodes, possessing a 1.24 F cm 2 maximum areal capacitance, good cyclic stability after 1000 cycles, as well as a 0.44 mWh cm 2 maximum energy density. The proposed approach in this study provides an idea to design and fabricate advanced electrodes for asymmetric devices in industrial energy-storage applications, which can be operated in large voltage windows with enhanced energy-power characteristics. title: Tunable interlayer spacings Ti3C2Tx MXene Ni C for enhanced electromagnetic microwave absorption
authors: Jingyu Song, Yongqian Shen, Guibin Zhang, Mingxuan Sun, Mengyao Han, Xueyan Du
abstract: While two-dimensional lamellar materials, specifically Ti3C2Tx MXenes, have shown great promise as wave-absorbing materials, the precise design of interlayer spacing poses a persistent challenge. In this study, Ti3C2Tx MXene layers with adjustable interlayer spacings were crafted using a straightforward molecular welding technique. Through the incorporation of Ni nanoparticles onto the Ti3C2Tx MXene layers using a combination of simple mechanical stirring and carbonation reactions, we successfully developed Ti3C2Tx MXene Ni C composites featuring a distinct lamellar structure. A uniform dispersion of Ni nanoparticles on the surface of the Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets was found with some of the nanoparticles intercalated into the layers. The Ti3C2Tx MXene Ni C composites exhibited a maximum reflection loss (RL) value of 42.3 dB at 12.3 GHz, accompanied by an impressive effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.6 GHz. This outstanding absorption performance could be attributed to various factors, including the dielectric loss of the Ti3C2Tx MXene lamellae, reflections and scattering of multiphase heterostructures, the magnetic loss of the Ni nanoparticles, and their synergistic attenuation. Furthermore, Ni nanoparticles with high electrical conductivity induced vortex currents under the alternating influence of electromagnetic waves (EMWs), resulting in a substantial depletion. This study introduces an innovative approach for synthesizing Ti3C2Tx MXene Ni C composites with tunable interlayer spacing, showing their potential for applications in microwave absorption (MA).
conclusion: 4 Conclusion In this study, xDA-Ti 3 C 2 with controllable layer spacing was prepared via a dehydration condensation reaction between xDA and NH 2 functionalized Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers. Subsequently, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Ni C composites with unique layered structures were prepared using a simple mechanical stirring and carbonization strategy. Compared to traditional MAs, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Ni C composites retained the accordion structure of pure Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene. The increase in layer spacing exposes the material to a wider interface, preventing agglomeration and providing a favorable interface for subsequent nickel metal doping. Moreover, the electromagnetic parameters could be accurately controlled by changing the doping amount of Ni metal. Several highly dispersed magnetic particles are doped into the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet layer or attached to its surface, imparting the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet with magnetic characteristics and significantly improving its magnetic loss capability. Finally, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Ni C composites exhibit excellent EMWs absorption performance (RL = 42.3 dB) owing to the synergistic effect of multicomponent complementary effects, conduction loss, interfacial polarization, and dielectric loss. Molecular welding offers an inimitable method for controlling the interlayer spacing between the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers and other two-dimensional materials, providing theoretical guidance for designing high-performance, two-dimensional wave-absorbing materials.

title: High-performance supercapacitors based on nonfunctionalized MXenes
authors: Ibrahim W. Lisheshar, Sina Rouhi, Feridun Ay, Nihan Kosku Perkgöz
abstract: MXenes are a group of two-dimensional materials that have attracted significant research interest worldwide due to their intriguing electrochemical characteristics for use in energy storage applications. However, the conductivity of MXenes and their performance as supercapacitor electrodes can be hindered by surface terminations. This study investigates the capability of non-functionalized MXenes, synthesized via chemical vapor deposition for use as supercapacitor electrodes, presenting a novel approach that explores the potential of these materials in energy storage applications. The synthesized MXenes are used to create supercapacitor electrodes, which are subjected to detailed analysis. The specific areal capacitance (SAC) of these electrodes (48.6 nm thick) is found to be 39.5 mFcm 2 at a scan rate of 2 mVs 1, equivalent to 928.4 Fg-1. Further investigation using galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) analysis reveals an initial specific gravimetric capacitance (SGC) of 442.6 Fg-1 at a current density of 0.5 Ag-1, which progressively decreases to 13.4 Fg-1 at 10 Ag-1. Remarkably, the MXene supercapacitors exhibit excellent stability over 10,000 charge-discharge cycles, retaining 85 of their initial capacitance. These findings contribute to our understanding of MXene-based energy storage devices and pave the way for practical applications in high-performance supercapacitors.
conclusion: In conclusion, our study shows the synthesis of nonfunctional-group-terminated MXenes using CVD, and extensive characterization utilizing multiple spectroscopic and microscopic approaches. The outcomes demonstrate that both the MXene coverage on the substrate and the thickness of MXene flakes increase with the synthesis temperature. The effectiveness of the MXene electrodes as supercapacitors was assessed utilizing an aqueous electrolyte solution, CPS, or CGS. The devices showed an overall amazing SGC performance when the impact of increasing MXene s thickness on its performance as a supercapacitor electrode was examined. It was also determined that higher coverage samples performed better, according to research on the impact of the MXene coverage area. This work provides valuable insights into the unique potential of pristine MXenes as innovative high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors, highlighting their promise in advancing energy storage technologies. It is worth noting that pseudo active materials like conductive polymers, and metal oxides possess high surface areas due to pseudo capacitance, and hence can improve supercapacitor performance if hybridized with other materials like MXenes. Like with Ti3 C2 Tx , CVD MXenes are also able to hybridize with these high surface area materials, which is a possibility worth exploring. CRediT authorship contribution statement Ibrahim W. title: High-capacity Zn-ion storage in NiMnHCF Ti3C2Tx MXene composite cathode boosted by Mn-containing electrolyte for aqueous Zn-ion hybrid capacitors
authors: Kun Fang, Jingyuan Zhang, Jianing Yu, Yuting Hu, Jiawei Wang, Zhuo Wang, Bin Zhao
abstract: Zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors (Zn-ion HSCs), combining battery-type cathodes and capacitor-type anodes, present a promising solution for large-scale energy storage. Nonetheless, the rational design of cathode materials with high capacity and long cycle life remains a significant challenge. In this work, binder-free NiMn0.1-hexacyanoferrate MXene (NiMn0.1HCF MXene) composite electrodes, characterized by ultrasmall HCF nanoparticles, were fabricated via the self-assembly of Ti3C2Tx MXene (MX) and ultrathin layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets, followed by in-situ LDH conversion and ultrasonic spraying onto on carbon cloth (CC). By leveraging the nanoscale NiMn0.1HCF, the seamless integration with conductive MX, and the electrolyte-driven conversion reaction of Zn4SO4 (OH)6 xH2O (ZSH) with Mn2+, the composite achieves a specific capacitance of 1548.7 F g 1 (387.1 mA h g 1) at 1 A g 1 in a 1 M ZnSO4 and 0.1 M MnSO4 electrolyte, with 77.82 capacity retention over 15,000 cycles at 5 A g 1. Moreover, when assembled into a Zn-ion HSC, the NiMn0.1HCF MX delivers an impressive energy density of 62.8 Wh kg 1 and a high power density of 10.1 kW kg 1 at 1.8 V, retaining 95.6 of its initial capacitance after 25,000 cycles at 1 A g 1. In-situ and ex-situ characterization reveal the reversible insertion extraction of H+ Zn2+ in the cathode and the reversible conversion between ZSH and ZnxMnO(OH)2 (ZMO), which jointly contribute to the exceptional capacity and decent cycling stability. This work lays a foundation for designing high-performance HCF cathode materials and advancing high-capacity aqueous Zn-ion HSCs.
conclusion: In summary, we have developed binder-free NiMn0.1 HCF MX CC composite electrodes for high-performance aqueous Zn-ion HSCs. The composite electrodes, featuring small HCF nanoparticles and Mn doping, demonstrate impressive electrochemical performance. The integration of MX nanosheets and the in-situ conversion of LDH into NiMn0.1 HCF contribute to enhanced charge transfer and ion transport, resulting in a high specific capacitance of 1548.7F g 1 (387.1 mA h g 1 ) at 1 A g 1 and excellent cycling stability, with 77.82 capacity retention after 15,000 cycles at 5 A g 1 . Furthermore, the assembled NiMn0.1 HCF MXene CC AC Zn-ion HSC delivers a remarkable energy density of 62.8 Wh kg 1 and a high power density of 10.1 kW kg 1 , while retaining 95.6 of its initial capacitance after 25,000 cycles at 1 A g 1 . In-depth characterization reveals that the synergistic contributions of ZSH dissolution-deposition conversion and co-insertion extraction of Zn2+ H+ are crucial for achieving high specific capacitance and long-term cycling stability. These findings not only provide valuable insights into the design of high-performance HCF cathode materials but also pave the way for the development of high-capacity, durable aqueous Zn-ion HSCs. title: Assembly of flexible Ti3C2Tx fiber with promoted ionic transport by constructing hierarchical flakes size for high-performance fiber shaped supercapacitors
authors: Yang Zhang, Xiangxiang Pi, Jian Xu, Kangxin Qi, Shenao Zhang, Yusen Wang, Qingqing Tang, Diwei Gu, Bin Sun, Xianan Qin, Wangyang Lu
abstract: With the booming development of wearable system, the flexible fiber-shaped supercapacitor (FSC) has received sufficient attention. However, impeding by the sinuous electrolyte diffusion pathway and limited surface area, the fiber electrode usually causes low energy density and mediocre rate capability. Here, small-sized Ti3C2Tx MXene (s-M) intercalated Ti3C2Tx flakes (s-M M) fiber is constructed by microfluidic spinning method. Encouragingly, the existence of s-M flakes can prevent the layer restacking of adjacent Ti3C2Tx sheets significantly, constructing porous architectures for fast ion diffusion and exposing abundant active sites for ion adsorption. Moreover, due to homogeneous crosslink via hydrogen bond, s-M M fiber appears stable interface coupling, which imparts fast electron migration and excellent deformation endurance. As a result, the s-M M fiber displays huge mass-capacitance (271.35 F g 1 at 1 A g 1), good rate performance (197.92 F g 1 at 10 A g 1) and outstanding long-term cycling properties (80.7 capacitance retention after 10000 cycling). More importantly, matching with the graphene fiber, the asymmetrical FSC shows large capacitance of 62.98 F g 1 at 0.1 A g 1, high energy density and favorable deformation ability. This work raises an effective strategy for the design of high-performance FSC and the application in wearable system.
conclusion: In summary, flexible s-M M fiber was constructed by microfluidic spinning method for wearable system. Intercalating s-M between the Ti3 C2 Tx flakes can impede the re-stacking effect effectively, leading to rich adsorption sites and abundant diffusion channels. Besides, the homogeneous architecture allows to construct a stable crosslink between s-M and Ti3 C2 Tx flakes, achieving good interface coupling and high conductivity for fibrous electrode. As a result, the s-M M fiber appears outstanding electrochemical performance, such as large capacitance (271.35 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 ), favorable rate properties (197.92 F g 1 at 10 A g 1 ) and admired cycling stability (80.7 capacitance retention after 10000 cycling). Also, the assembled FSC, matching s-M M fiber with graphene fiber, presents good reversible capacitance (62.98 F g 1 at 0.1 A g 1 ), high energy density and unrivalled mechanical endurance (98.6 capacitance retention after 100 times bending). More importantly, the FSC can drive the LED electronics stably, providing considerable application potential in wearable system. title: A compressible asymmetric supercapacitor based on carbon Felt MWCNT PANI and MXene
authors: Elif Vargun, Haojie Fei, Ulku Anik, Qilin Cheng, Petr Saha
abstract: Compressible supercapacitors are novel energy storage devices for commercial portable and flexible electronics. Substantial efforts have been made to develop compressible supercapacitors with high voltage output, good mechanical stability, and electrochemical performance. This study investigates the performance of a compressible asymmetric supercapacitor configuration based on a polyaniline-modified carbon felt multi-walled carbon nanotube composite (a-CF MWCNT PANI) as the positive electrode and a titanium carbide-MXene (Ti3C2Tx) as the negative electrode. The acid-functionalized MWCNTs were loaded into activated carbon felt by dipping and drying and subsequently were coated by polyaniline via the chemical oxidation polymerization method. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed the formation of the dendritic structure of PANI on the surface of 3D porous composite (a-CF MWCNT PANI) positive electrode. X-ray diffraction (XRD), SEM, and cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements revealed 2D layered morphology and pseudocapacitive behavior of Ti3C2Tx-MXene. The specific capacitance of the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor was found as 1.6 F cm 2 at 5 mA cm 2, the corresponding energy density and power density were 262 μWh cm 2 and 2.7 mW cm 2, respectively. The asymmetric cell exhibited a retention rate of 92.4 after 1000 cycles. Above 50 strain, the supercapacitor showed a favorable CV profile, which is owing to the enhanced electrical conductivity of the CF composite electrode caused by compression. The capacitance retention retained more than 90 over 200 compression-recovery cycles.
conclusion: An effective compressible asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated using a-CF MWCNT PANI positive electrode and a Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene negative electrode. Both XPS and FTIR spectroscopy confirm that the first MWCNTs were loaded into a-CF, and then PANI functionalization of a-CF MWCNT was performed successfully. With MWCNTs and PANI coatings, the electric conductivity and specific capacitance of the positive electrode were significantly increased. For the MXene negative electrode, a successful etching of aluminum from MAX phase was verified by XRD analysis. Moreover, SEM analysis demonstrated flake-like morphologies of 2D MXene nanosheets. By the asymmetric configuration, the cell voltage of the assembled supercapacitor was extended to 1.3 V. The specific capacitance was found as 1.6 F cm 2 at 5 mA cm 2 , the corresponding energy density and power density were 262 μWh cm 2 and 2.7 mW cm 2 , respectively. The asymmetric cell exhibited an excellent retention rate of 92.4 after 1000 GCD cycles. Moreover, the asymmetric cell became compressible due to the compressibility of CF, and the capacitance retention retained more than 90 over 200 compression-recovery cycles. Considering the preparation procedure, it is possible to conclude that, as a result, a practical, economical, and robust compressible asymmetric supercapacitor was developed.
