title: Synergistically coupling of 3D FeNi-LDH arrays with Ti3C2Tx-MXene nanosheets toward superior symmetric supercapacitor
authors: Renjie Zhang, Jidong Dong, Wei Zhang, Lina Ma, Zaixing Jiang, Jiajun Wang, Yudong Huang
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are promising energy materials for their considerable theoretical capacities and adjustable compositions, however, also subjected to the intrinsic poor conductivity and agglomeration property, hence, the precise hybridization with high conductivity and active surface matrix is an effective strategy to solve these intractable problems. Herein, we exploit hierarchical nanohybrids via ionic hetero-assembly of 3D FeNi-LDH arrays on 2D Ti3C2Tx-based MXene nanosheets through mutual coupling synergy. The strong interfacial interaction and good electronic coupling between the FeNi-LDH arrays and Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets not only improve the structural stability, electrical conductivity, and electrolyte-accessibility but also greatly boost the redox reaction kinetics. The obtained Fe1Ni3-LDH Ti3C2Tx-MXene energy materials reveal prominent conductivity, superior capacitance behavior, and the constructed symmetric supercapacitor demonstrates outstanding energy densities of 94.1 Wh Kg-1 and power density of 7431.8 W Kg-1. This study offers a facile and efficient strategy for developing 2D MXene-based energy storage devices with a stable interface and favorable electrochemical performance.
conclusion: In summary, 3D FeNi-LDH Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanohybrids were successfully prepared via an electrostatic attraction connection of negatively charged 2D Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets with positively charged FeNi-LDH arrays. In this architecture, the high conductivity Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets not only can construct a successive conductive network but also act as the platform for the growth of FeNi-LDH arrays, ensuring the superb electrical conductivity of the whole energy materials. As a result, the optimized battery-type electrode Fe1 Ni3 -LDH Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene indicates remarkable rate capability, the outstanding gravimetric capacitance for 922.6 F g-1 , and retains for 88 after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the symmetric supercapacitor based on Fe1 Ni3 -LDH Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene electrodes can exhibit excellent electrochemical performance with a high energy density of 94.1 Wh kg-1 at a power density of 802.4 W kg-1 . These superior electrochemical performances are benefited from the high capacity of Fe1 Ni3 -LDH arrays, excellent conductivity of the Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets and their synergistically interactive effect in the heterostructure. This strategy not only proves the feasibility of the development of the desirable Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene, but also paves the way for the fabrication of the hybrids electrodes with a stable interface for high-performance supercapacitors. title: In situ synthesis of M (Fe, Cu, Co and Ni)-MOF MXene composites for enhanced specific capacitance and cyclic stability in supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Yaxiong Ji, Weibin Li, Yang You, Guihong Xu
abstract: In this study, an in situ method was developed to synthesize a series of uniform 3D MOFs (Fe-, Cu-, Co-, Ni)-BTC 2D MXene (Ti3C2Tx) composites, and the experimental results show that a typical sample of Ni-MOF MX 2 exhibits the highest specific capacitance of 1160.5 F g 1 and 736 F g 1 at a current density of 1 A g 1 and 20 A g 1, respectively, which is 2.3 times higher than the value of 320 F g 1 at a current density of 20 A g 1 on the bare Ni-MOF, and particularly maintains significant cyclic stability after 10,000 cycles at a high current density of 20 A g 1. The improved electrochemical performance is ascribed to the synergistic interaction between layered MXene and MOFs, which were evidenced by experiments and theoretical calculations. The Ni-MOF MX 2 AC asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device demonstrates a maximum energy density of 48.2 Wh kg 1 at 750 W kg 1. It retains 94 capacity after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the value still maintained at 23.3 Wh kg 1 when elevating power density to 15000 W kg 1. This indicates that the obtained MOF MXene composites are probably alternative materials for supercapacitor electrodes in energy storage.
conclusion: 4 Conclusion In summary, a series of MOF MXene composite materials were synthesized by a one-step in situ method. Intercalation of the MXene into the Co-MOF, Ni-MOF, Cu-MOF and Fe-MOF materials contributes to four types of surfaces: flower-like , rock , pomegranate seed and sponge surfaces, respectively, which contribute to different electrochemical performances. During the composite process, both Co and Ni ions are initially fixed on the surface of MXene through electrostatic interactions and serve as the centers for in-situ growth of MOFs, whereas Co ions offer stronger interaction with the suitable dosage of MXene layers. Uniform distribution of MXene on the surface of Co-MOF and Ni-MOF facilitates efficient ion transport channels and high charge transfer rates for supercapacitor applications. Among the various MOF MXene-based materials, Ni-MOF MX 2 shows outstanding properties with a high specific capacitance of 1160.5 F g 1 at a current density of 1 A g, and moreover maintains significant cyclic stability after 10,000 cycles at 20 A g. The Ni-MOF MX 2 AC ASC exhibits a maximum energy density of 48.2 Wh kg 1 at 750 W kg 1 and retains 94 of the initial capacity after 10,000 cycles. Both experimental and theoretical calculations have demonstrated that these excellent electrochemical performances are due to the synergistic effect between MXene nanosheets and unique structure of MOFs. Such prepared materials possibly shed a light on solving the key issues of MXene layer stacking, poor conductivity of MOFs, and the development of high-performance energy storage devices for their practical applications.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene and Vanadium nitride Porous carbon as electrodes for asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Sandhya Venkateshalu, Andrews Nirmala Grace
abstract: MXenes are the emerging class of 2D materials, widely explored as supercapacitor electrodes with their explicit properties. Using the pseudocapacitive nature of the widely reported MXene - Ti3C2Tx, an asymmetric cell is designed with Ti3C2Tx as the negative electrode and Vanadium nitride Porous carbon as the positive electrode. The asymmetric cell provides a high cell voltage of 1.8 V with a specific capacitance of 105 F g at 1 A g in 6 M KOH. It also presents a capacitance retention of 73 even after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles. The asymmetric cell exhibits a high potential window, which is about 3 times higher when compared to symmetric supercapacitors. The asymmetric electrode system exhibits an energy density of 12.81 Wh kg and a corresponding power density of 985.8 W kg at 1 A g. This value of energy density is greater when compared to various symmetric supercapacitors. Thus Ti3C2Tx MXene electrodes can effectively replace the conventional carbon electrodes used in asymmetric supercapacitors.
conclusion: In summary, this work reports on the testing of Ti3 C2 Tx as the negative electrode and VN PC as the positive electrode in an asymmetric cell. Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes were synthesized by etching the Al layers by immersing them in aqueous HF solutions and further delaminating them with DMSO. It is well known that the synthesis of Vanadium nitride is very difficult without the use of the dangerous ammonia gas. Herein, we have synthesized Vanadium nitride porous carbon through a simple and safe method using the data available in literature with modifications. In a 3-electrode system, Ti3 C2 Tx MXene and VN PC electrode exhibits specific capacitances of 283 F g and 52 F g at 0.5 A g respectively. VN PC Ti3 C2 Tx asymmetric 2-electrode cell exhibits a superior capcitance of 105 F g at 1 A g with energy density and power density of 12.81 Wh kg and 985.8 W kg respectively. The results show that the carbon used convetionally in asymmetric supercapacitors as negative electrode can be repaced with MXene electrodes. title: Optimizing the electron spin state of hierarchical NiCo2O4 MXene LDH 3D composite electrode by heterointerface engineering to enhance energy density and excellent cyclic stability of supercapacitor
authors: Jianghong You, Yiming Yuan, Chen Zhang, Haoming Xu, Mingyao Chen, Ying Wang, Dongsheng Chen
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
abstract: The transition metal oxide of nickel cobaltite (NiCo2O4) has gained more and more attention from battery industry for its excellent properties of high capacitance and cycling stability. However, its performance when used in supercapacitors is compromised due to its limited active sites and poor conductivity. Herein, a 3D (three-dimensional) hierarchical and high-performance material of NiCo2O4 MXene LDH (LDH: layered double hydroxide) composite was designed and synthesized. In the material, NiCo2O4 nanorods form a skeleton of nanosheet arrays on layered MXene; and on the nanosheet arrays, NiCo-LDH nanoparticles are attached to form a 3D hierarchical structure, extending the electrochemically active sites, suppressing the agglomeration of NiCo-LDH and producing hierarchical channels that promote electron and ion transport. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and the results of Ultraviolet visible (UV Vis) spectrophotometry indicated that the introduction of MXene and NiCo-LDH induces a redistribution of the electronic states of NiCo2O4 due to the formation of a heterointerface, thereby decreasing its bandgap by about 1.42 eV. The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis further demonstrated the negative shift in the initial binding energies of nickel (Ni) and cobalt (Co) atoms, which is due to their transition of spin states; and this is in agreement with the high intensity of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) peak in the NiCo2O4 MXene LDH composite. The in situ Raman analysis reveals that the enhanced energy storage performance originates from the accelerated formation and increased exposure of NiCoOOH active species during electrochemical cycling. The synergistic effect of MXene and NiCo-LDH introduced into NiCo2O4 enhanced the supercapacitor in terms of power and energy densities. It was indicated that the supercapacitor fabricated from NiCo2O4 MXene LDH supercapacitor exhibited a specific capacitance of 5066 F g 1 at 1 A g 1, and a capacitance retention of 97.82 after 10,000 charge cycles at 10 A g 1. Moreover, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device with a NiCo2O4 MXene LDH AC configuration was developed. The supercapacitor presented an energy density and power density of 70.11 Wh kg 1 and 850.22 W kg 1, respectively. The redistribution of electronic states and decreased bandgap could facilitate the creation of NiCo2O4-based materials with customized features for supercapacitors.
conclusion: In this work, we proposed and successfully constructed a three-dimensional hierarchical NiCo2 O4 MXene LDH (LDH: layered double hydroxide) composite electrode through rational heterointerface engineering to overcome the intrinsic limitations of NiCo2 O4 -based materials in supercapacitor applications. The strategy effectively integrates the advantages of NiCo2 O4 nanorods, conductive MXene nanosheets, and electrochemically active NiCo-LDH nanoparticles into a unified architecture, thereby achieving a well-interconnected structure with enhanced electron ion transport pathways and expanded electrochemical active surfaces. One of the key innovations of this study lies in the modulation of the electronic spin states and the redistribution of electronic states within the composite. DFT calculations, along with XPS, UV Vis, PL, and EPR characterizations, demonstrated that the introduction of MXene and NiCo-LDH triggered significant changes in the local electronic structure of Ni and Co atoms. This led to a considerable narrowing of the bandgap from 4.00 eV (pristine NiCo2 O4 ) to 2.58 eV (NiCo2 O4 MXene LDH), which facilitated improved electrical conductivity and charge transfer kinetics across the heterointerface. The in situ Raman analysis reveals that the enhanced energy storage performance originates from the accelerated formation and increased exposure of NiCoOOH active species during electrochemical cycling. Electrochemical measurements further confirmed the remarkable performance of the as-prepared composite. The NiCo2 O4 MXene LDH electrode exhibited an ultrahigh specific capacitance of 5066 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 , with excellent rate capability and long-term cycling stability (97.82 retention after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g 1 ). Moreover, the asymmetric supercapacitor device assembled with this composite delivered a superior energy density of 70.22 Wh kg 1 and a power density of 850.11 W kg 1 , outperforming many previously reported systems. This study not only demonstrates a successful pathway for optimizing transition metal oxide-based electrodes via electronic and interfacial engineering but also highlights the crucial role of spin state regulation and synergistic component design in improving electrochemical storage performance. The results suggest that the NiCo2 O4 MXene LDH composite holds significant promise for the development of high-performance, durable, and scalable supercapacitor devices. More broadly, the design principles and insights obtained herein can be extended to other functional materials and energy storage platforms. title: Multifunctional Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposites for integrated all solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors and energy-saving electrochemical systems of H2 production by urea and alcohols electrolysis
authors: Shidong Li, Jincheng Fan, Guocai Xiao, Shanqiang Gao, Kexin Cui, Zisheng Chao
abstract: Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposites have been fabricated by vacuum filtration and hydrothermal-annealing methods, and their electrochemical performance were investigated for energy storage and conversion, systematically. As electrode materials, Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposites in 6 M KOH solution demonstrated the specific capacitance of 240.1 F g 1 at 0.1 A g 1 and the long-term cycle stability. The solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors exhibited an operating potential window of 1.4 V, a specific capacitance of 97.9 F g 1at 0.25 A g 1, an energy density of 95.9 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 630.4 W kg 1, and excellent long-term durability. Furthermore, the connected solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors inseries and parallels presented the promising practical applications. Besides, Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx nanocomposites displayed outstanding catalytic behaviors for energy-saving H2 generation by urea and alcohols electrolysis. The electrolyzer in KOH + CH3CH2OH electrolyte required only 1.33 V potential to deliver the current density of 0.5 A g 1. Especially, the elctrochemical system of H2 production by The electrolyzer and the powered solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors based on Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx nanocomposites was constructed, demonstrating outstanding properties of H2 production. Therefore, this study not only shows enormous potential of Co3O4 Ti3C2Tx nanocomposites as a portable power supply but also indicates its great opportunities in energy-saving H2 production in practical applications.
conclusion: In summary, Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanocomposites have been prepared by vacuum filtration and hydrothermal-annealing methods and their structural and electrochemical performances were investigated, systematically, for energy storage and conversion. Co3 O4 nanomaterials (nanoparticles and nanorods) randomly distributed on the surfaces or between the layers of Ti3 C2 Tx . As the electrode materials for supercapacitors, Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites presented the outstanding specific capacitances and cyclic stability. Further, the constructed solid-state supercapacitor of S NaOH-025 AC achieves an operating potential window of 1.4 V, a specific capacitance of 97.9 F g 1 at 0.25 A g 1 , an energy density of 95.9 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 630.4 W kg 1 , and excellent long-term durability. The ASCs can be easily connected into series or parallel for high voltage and current, demonstrating excellent electrochemical properties of energy storage for practical applications. Besides, Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites presented outstanding catalytic behaviors for H2 generation in various electrolytes and the introductions of urea or alcohols, replacing OER by the UOR and MOR, are the ideal energy-saving methods for H2 production from water. Remarkably, the electrolyzer with S NaOH-05 in KOH + CH3 CH2 OH electrolyte required only 1.33 V potential to deliver the current density of 0.5 A g 1 . Especially, the electrolyzer with Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites as electrochemical electrode and powered Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites AC ACS can be assembled electrochemical system in for H2 production. Therefore, this study not only shows enormous potential of Co3 O4 Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites as a portable power supply, but also indicates its great opportunities in energy-saving H2 production in practical applications.

title: Perovskite structured LaMnO3 nanoparticles adorned on the MXene 2D sheets: An innovative crossbreed electrode material for robust supercapacitor application and oxygen evolution reactions
authors: M. Murugesan, K.R. Nagavenkatesh, P. Devendran, N. Nallamuthu, Y.C. Sunilkumar
abstract: This study aimed to address energy demand constraints by developing a novel hybrid electrode material for energy storage and conversion, perovskite structured lanthanum manganite (LaMnO3) with MXene composites. The LaMnO3 NPs decorated on the MXene nanosheets were synthesized by simple hydrothermal technique. The synthesized lanthanum-based MXene nanocomposite (NCs) was examined by Structural, morphological and spectroscopic analysis using XRD, HR-TEM, SEM with EDX, FTIR and XPS tools. Through the electrochemical analysis, the perovskite structured LaMnO3 NPs and LaMnO3 MXene NCs were achieved remarkable specific capacitance (Csp) of 782.70 and 1216.36F gat 5 mV s respectively. The prepared LaMnO3 MXene NCs proved outstanding capacitance retaining 90.1 after 5000 cycles. Besides, a Asymmetric supercapacitor (ACS) device was built with MXene and LaMnO3 MXene electrodes, which is shows a remarkable power density (PD) 1350 W kg with corresponding energy density (ED) 150.6 Wh kg and it displays the remarkable cycling stability up to 77.6 was retained after 5000 cycles at 10 A g. In addition from Oxygen evaluation reaction analysis the LaMnO3 MXene composite exhibits overpotential of 446.10 mV corresponding to the 10 mA cm2 current density, along with the lesser Tafel slope of 88.31 mV dec for OER in 1 M KOH. As a result, the prepared LaMnO3 MXene electrode having exceptional qualities might prove towards the trustable electrode for the advance supercapacitors and water splitting applications.
conclusion: The rhombohedral structure of LaMnO3 MXene composite was successfully synthesized using a simple hydrothermal process and the resultant samples were analysed with numerous characterization. It confirmed by structural morphological, functional group and elemental composition via, XRD, HR-TEM, SEM, FTIR, XPS and EDX with mapping studies. From the electrochemical evaluation, the outstanding capacitive behaviour of LaMnO3 MXene was confirmed by using their pseudocapacitor nature of CV profile, that is attained Csp of 1216F g at 5 mV s. Finally, the ASC device is built with synthesized rhombohedral structure LaMnO3 MXene composite as cathode and MXene as the anode electrode. The greater efficiency Csp of 136.13F g at 5 mV s is demonstrated by this novel asymmetric supercapacitor technology. It also has excellent ED and PD of 150 Wh kg and 1350 W kg, respectively. The device exhibited excellent cycling stability, retaining up to 77.6 of its capacitance after 5000 cycles. The prepared LaMnO3 MXene structure electrode offering excellent OER performance with the low overpotential of 446.10 mV and Tafel slopes 88.31 mV dec in 1 M KOH. For effective energy storage and conversion applications, the suggested module to assemble the perovskite oxide nanoparticle-decorated MXene sheets would therefore be the appropriate materials. It is unequivocally demonstrates the trustable novel type electrode for energy storage and energy conversion applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement M. Murugesan: Investigation. K.R. title: Novel synthesis of B-doped Ti3C2Tx thin sheets via BF3 Lewis acid etching: Structural insights and Supercapacitor applications
authors: Jeremiah Hao Ran Huang, Anil A. Kashale, Shih-Wen Tseng, Jui-Chin Lee, I-Wen Peter Chen
abstract: The rising demand for energy storage spurs research on supercapacitor materials, valued for high-power density and long-term cycling, vital in industries. Among two-dimensional materials, MXene, with a general formula of Mn+1XnTx, where M represents early transition metals, X indicates C and or N, Tx represents functionalized surface groups, and n = 1, 2, or 3, stands out as an ideal candidate for energy storage applications. Here, for the first time, we report the use of a Lewis acid, boron trifluoride (BF3), as an electron-deficient etchant in a sulfuric acid (H2SO4) solution for etching aluminum from the model system Ti3AlC2 MAX (M: transition metals, A: Al, X: carbon.), resulting in the formation of B-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene. Ex-Situ electrochemical X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis showed reversible (002) plane changes in B-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene, from 5.72 to 7.0 , indicating ions intercalation and deintercalation, a first-time demonstration of significant ion transportation. Such fundamental insight determines that the specific capacitance of B-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene has found to be 396 F g at current density of 1 A g. This research introduces a novel synthesis approach aimed at understanding microstructural transformations of B-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene during electrochemical processes. This contributes to the advancement of MXene-based materials for future electrochemical applications.
conclusion: In this study, we successfully developed the first effective Lewis acid, BF3 , as etchant was demonstrated. A distinctive feature of the B-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene is the presence of B, F, and O-related functional groups on its surface, greatly enriching its electrochemical properties. Electrochemical analysis revealed that B-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene possesses commendable specific capacitance values of 396 F g at a current density of 1 A g, which are superior to or comparable with the state-of-the art MXene results. Additionally, ex-situ electrochemical XRD analysis distinctly demonstrated the expansion and contraction of interlayer distances in B-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene during the electrochemical process, as well as the transitional states, highlighting the relationship between H+ intercalation-induced lattice changes in acidic electrolytes. Furthermore, the observation of low charge transfer resistance in a two-electrode symmetric capacitor indicates the good electrical conductivity of B-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, presenting a novel method for creating B-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with unique chemical characteristics. This discovery paves the way for future electrochemical applications.

title: Advanced aqueous sodium hybrid supercapacitors based on plant waste-derived activated carbon anode and multilayered Ti3C2 MXene cathode
authors: Tetiana Boichuk, Andrii Boichuk, Mahesh Eledath Changarath, Marie Krečmarová, Rafael Abargues, Vitalii Vashchynskyi, Saïd Agouram, Juan F. Sánchez-Royo
abstract: Hybrid sodium supercapacitors are emerging as highly promising energy storage devices for current and future applications in high-power electronics and the automotive industry. However, pushing their performance to competitive levels requires the development of innovative electrode material combinations to simultaneously enhance specific energy and power while significantly reducing energy production costs. Here, we report the first demonstration of an aqueous sodium supercapacitor employing an asymmetric electrode configuration with multilayered Ti3C2Tx MXene as the cathode and plant waste-derived activated carbon (AC) as the anode. In contrast to MXene Carbon composite electrodes, already described in the literature, our system relies on asymmetric pairing of different electrode materials, exploiting their respective pseudocapacitive (MXene) and electric double-layer (AC) charge accumulation mechanisms. The device achieves a specific capacitance of 155 Ah kg, a high energy density of 57 Wh kg, and a power density of 2110 W kg. These metrics are maintained over 5000 charge-discharge cycles, demonstrating excellent stability, rate performance, and Coulombic efficiency. The use of eco-friendly and low-cost AC from plant waste as an anode, in synergy with pseudocapacitive multilayered Ti3C2Tx as cathode material, offers a sustainable route toward efficient energy storage systems, demonstrating the potential of this electrode combination in practical supercapacitor applications.
conclusion: In summary, a combination of electrodes based on multilayered Ti3 C2 MXene and AC was used in high-performance aqueous sodium hybrid supercapacitors. The successful selective etching of the high-quality MAX phase allowed us to obtain multilayered MXene with high values of specific capacity in aqueous sodium electrolyte and excellent performance under high current conditions. Moreover, the compatibility of multilayered Ti3 C2 with mesoporous AC extracted from plant waste leads to the development of a safe, stable, and efficient sodium hybrid supercapacitor with a capacity of about 155 mAh g, excellent energy (57 Wh kg) and power density (2110 W kg). Long-term cycling of coin cells CR 2032 based on this electrode combination shows high operating stability and specific properties retention even during 1000 cycles, emphasizing its potential for future integration into high-performance commercial hybrid supercapacitors. title: A novel strategy for high energy density supercapacitors: Formation of cyanuric acid between Ti3C2Tx (MXene) interlayer hybrid electrodes
authors: Chao Feng, Bingzhe Jia, Han Wang, Yan Wang, Xinming Wu
abstract: Ti3C2Tx (MXene) are attractive for electrode materials because of their high electrical conductivity, abundant interlayer ions and low density. However, the low energy density hinders its commercial application. Herein, a novel N-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene is synthesized by introducing a small organic molecule dicyandiamide (DCD) to tune the complex terminals. DCD can be inserted into the layers of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets while forming melamine by catalyst-free trimerization reaction. Then, melamine is converted into gt-C3N4 through high-temperature sintering. Finally, gt-C3N4 is oxidized to cyanuric acid (CA) through simple hydrothermal reaction. The prepared Ti3C2Tx CA composite electrode exhibits up to 4.8 at. nitrogen doping and has a stable triazine ring structure. It is also shown that the Ti3C2Tx CA composite electrode has high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability. More notably, it achieves an energy density of 51.1 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 2000 W kg 1, which exceeds the energy density of MXene based electrodes reported in the current literature. This excellent performance is attributed to the unique hydroxyl structure of the CA terminal and the excellent symmetry of CA in the composite electrode. In aqueous electrolytes, CA can form short chains during charging and the formation of short chains enables the storage of electrons and further provides a large number of new pseudocapacitive reaction sites for MXene. At the same time, the high electronegativity of the N and O atoms in CA also increases the electric double layer capacitor of the composite electrode to a certain extent, thus resulting in a high energy density of the composite electrode.
conclusion: during the formation of Ti3 C2 Tx CA composite electrode, CA replaced the -F group that does not participate in the pseudocapacitive reaction, but did not change the original OH and -O groups, and the pseudo capacitance of MXene was fully retained [13,21 23,45] . In addition, thanks to the unique hydroxyl structure of CA terminal and symmetry of CA, CA can form short chains during charging in aqueous electrolytes and the formation of short chains can realize the storage of electrons. At the same time, the formation of short chains further provides a large number of new pseudocapacitive reaction sites for MXene and the highly electronegative N and O atoms in CA also improve the electric double layer capacitor of the composite electrode to a certain extent. Therefore, the energy density of Ti3 C2 Tx CA composite electrode (51.1 Wh kg 1 ) is much higher than that of Ti3 C2 Tx electrode (29.7 Wh kg 1 ) (Fig. 5 (e), Table S3 and Table S4 ). 4 Conclusions In summary, we synthesized a novel highly N-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene through multi-step reaction by introducing small organic molecules, dicyandiamide, into the interlayer of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Benefiting from the unique hydroxyl structure and symmetry of CA terminal, CA enables charge storage by forming short chains, providing new pseudocapacitive reaction sites and higher bilayer capacitance. The prepared Ti3 C2 Tx CA composite electrode has a high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability. More notably, it achieves an amazing energy density of 51.1 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 2000 W kg 1 , which exceeds the energy density of MXene based electrode reported in the current literature. This work provides a new idea for the design of commercial MXene based electrodes by the method of Ti3 C2 Tx doping with small organic molecules.

title: High-performance flexible supercapacitor based on PEDOT:PSS wrapped delaminated Ti3C2Tx composite: Experimental and DFT validation
authors: Gourab Nandy, Swati Shaw, Subhradip Ghosh, Ashok Kumar Dasmahapatra
abstract: Exploring new electrode materials with cyclic stability and energy storage capacity is crucial for high-performance energy storage in portable electronics. Herein, we present PEDOT:PSS (PP) delaminated MXene (d-Ti3C2Tx) binary nanocomposites for electrode material for flexible supercapacitor (FSC). PP d-Ti3C2Tx (1:2 wt ratio, P1M2) on activated carbon cloth results in an excellent specific capacitance of 718.67 F g 1 at a current density of 3.5 A g 1 in 1 M H2SO4. PEDOT chains wrap the d-Ti3C2Tx nanosheets by an opposite electrostatic interaction, while PSS chains act as web-like carrier pathways between two adjacent nanosheets. First principle DFT simulations demonstrate that charge storage in PEDOT:PSS Ti3C2Tx is enhanced compared to PEDOT Ti3C2Tx, which describes the effect of PSS chains in the composite. Computationally obtained absorption spectra align well with experimental results, validating the proposed morphology. To employ the P1M2 electrode for FSC, P1M2-P1M2 symmetric solid-state supercapacitor (SSC) and P1M2-rGO asymmetric solid-state supercapacitor (ASC) have been fabricated using 1 M PVA-H2SO4 gel electrolyte. P1M2-P1M2 SSC and P1M2-rGO ASC exhibit a high specific capacitance of 260.23 F g 1 (0.5 A g 1) and 176.46 F g 1 (0.1 A g 1) receptively. Larger potential window, excellent specific capacitance retention of 89 for 5000 GCD cycles, and great performance retention over the bending and twisting conditions make the ASC device a marvelous candidate for the portable energy storage device. The ASC device shows change in specific energy (specific power) from 35.29 W h kg 1 (240 W kg 1) to 26.22 W h kg 1 (1200 W kg 1). An assembly of three such ASC devices glows a red LED for 2 min.
conclusion: In this work, we have adequately synthesized delaminated Ti3 C2 Tx (d-Ti3 C2 Tx ) by a low-cost method, integrating the mixed acid etching method followed by DMSO intercalation. Furthermore, PP d-Ti3 C2 Tx binary composites have been prepared with different ratios by the solvent mixing method and coated on the flexible activated carbon cloth. The conformation of the prepared composites was validated by several characterization techniques such as XRD, RAMAN, UV Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and FETEM. In three electrodes electrochemical performance PP, and d-Ti3 C2 Tx with a ratio 1:2 respectively (P1M2) exhibit great results in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The P1M2 electrode shows a brilliant specific capacitance value of 741. 23 F g 1 at a scan rate of 5 mV s, and 718. 67 F g 1 at a current density of 3. 5 A g 1 . P1M2 electrode shows brilliant E s 35. 93 Whkg 1 (at P s 1049. 90 Wkg-1 ), and 5. 68 Whkg 1 (at Ps 5996. 48 Wkg-1 ). Detailed DFT calculations confirmed that the charge transfer is doubled in the case of PEDOT:PSS Ti3 C2 Tx in comparison to PEDOT Ti3 C2 Tx . The charges flow from PEDOT and MXene to PSS. Consequently, PSS possesses the electron-rich region. The DFT calculated solar absorption spectrum for PEDOT:PSS, Ti3 C2 Tx , and PEDOT:PSS Ti3 C2 Tx agree very well with the experiments. Such excellent agreement substantiates the proposed morphology of the composite i.e. PEDOT wrapped d-Ti3 C2 Tx , aided by multiple PSS carrier pathways. For a flexible and wearable electronic device, we prepared a P1M2-P1M2 SSC and a P1M2-rGO ASC assembly using a gel electrolyte (PVA-H2 SO4 ). The highest specific capacitance has been achieved at 260. 23 F g 1 (at 0. 5 A g 1 ) by the P1M2-P1M2 SSC device; whereas P1M2-rGO ASC has a value of 176. 46 F g 1 (at 0. 1 A g 1 ). The specific energy (specific power) was from 13. 01 Whkg 1 (600 Wkg-1 ) to 2. 63 Whkg 1 (12035 Wkg-1 ) for the SSC device; and from 35. 29 Whkg 1 (240 Wkg-1 ) to 26. 22 Whkg 1 (1200 Wkg-1 ) for ASC device. Both SSC and ASC exhibit excellent performance over various bending and twisting cycles, ASC can operate in a larger potential window and longer durations at low current regions. Moreover, the ASC device shows excellent specific capacitance retention of 89.03 for 5000 GCD cycles. Subsequently, a red LED was glowed using three ASC devices in series. Hence the P1M2 electrode possesses enormous potential to be used in portable and wearable electronics. title: Ni nanorods with various morphologies on the surface of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets accelerate alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction
authors: Zengkun You, Kai Ou, Tian Tang, Yajing Cui, Wenting Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, Yudong Xia, Hongyan Wang
abstract: Under the background of sustainable energy development, the development of efficient, stable and low-cost electrocatalysts to improve electrochemical performance has become a research hotspot in the field of energy conversion. In this work, upright, one-fold and oblique Ni nanorods were designed and grown on Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets via glancing angle deposition technique of physical vapor deposition. For the hydrogen evolution reaction, the composite Ti3C2Tx upright exhibited a low overpotential of only 131 mV 10 mA cm2, along with excellent 24 h stability in 1 M KOH. Its excellent performance is mainly attributed to the high porosity of the upright nanorods, the fast electron transport channels provided by Ti3C2Tx MXene, and the stable interface structure. This research provides new ideas for constructing high-performance electrocatalytic catalysts and achieving efficient electrocatalytic conversion in sustainable energy systems.
conclusion: 4 Conclusion In this study, through the simple GLDA technique, precise morphology control was carried out on the surface of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene, and upright one-fold oblique nanorod-coated electrodes were grown. Among the fabricated electrodes, Ti 3 C 2 T x upright exhibited excellent HER performance, showing a low overpotential of only 131 mV at 10 mA cm 2 and remarkable catalytic stability. Both experimental and theoretical analysis demonstrate that the Ti 3 C 2 T x and Ni nanorod heterojunction structure enhances electron transfer, offers a relatively large reaction area, and increases the effective active sites for water splitting and hydrogen desorption. The electrode produced in this study exhibit excellent economic efficiency and broader applicability, providing a novel approach for designing high-performance, non-precious metal HER catalysts. Meanwhile, this technology is expected to be able to produce low-cost and high-performance HER catalysts on a large scale in the future.

title: Fabrication of MXene reduced graphene oxide MoO3 film electrode for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Ruidong Li, Lihua Chen, Shuxin Song, Bingyue Zheng, Tingxi Li, Wenhui Zheng, Yong Ma
abstract: MXene nanosheets exhibit a tendency to agglomerate in electrochemical processes, significantly impairing the electrochemical performance and diminishes their practical applicability. However, this problem can be effectively suppressed by introducing functional intercalation materials. Herein, MXene reduced graphene oxide (rGO) MoO3 films synthesized utilizing a vacuum-assisted filtration technique. MoO3 nanofibers and rGO nanosheets serve as essential intercalation materials, establishing a highly stable interlayer configuration within MXene nanosheets. This arrangement significantly increases the spacing between the MXene layers, thereby facilitating the development of a multidimensional and efficient ion transport pathway and exposing more active sites. Under the synergistic effect of this composite structure, the film exhibited a specific capacitance of 854.2 F g 1 at 1 A g 1. In addition, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) assembled with MXene rGO MoO3 film as the positive electrode and activated carbon (AC) as the negative electrode shows a wide voltage window of 1.6 V and achieves a high energy density of 54 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 800 W kg 1. More importantly, at 3 A g 1, this ASC maintained 85.4 capacitance retention after 14,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent cycling stability. The optimization strategy for the MXene rGO MoO3 electrode not only illustrates the technological progress of MXene within the domain of energy storage but also establishes a robust technological framework and theoretical underpinning for its utilization in flexible energy storage devices.
conclusion: 3 Conclusions Herein, MoO 3 nanowires and rGO nanosheets were synthesized utilizing hydrothermal and ascorbic acid reduction techniques, respectively. Following this, MXene, MXene rGO, and MXene rGO MoO 3 films were effectively produced through vacuum-assisted filtration. The incorporation of MoO 3 and rGO significantly improved the ion transport pathways within the films and augmented the ionic active sites of MXene, resulting in remarkable electrochemical characteristics. Notably, the electrochemical properties of the MXene rGO MoO 3 film are particularly exceptional, achieving a specific capacitance of 854.2 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 . An ASC was constructed based on the high-performance MXene rGO MoO 3 film. This device demonstrated a voltage window of up to 1.6 V and maintained a capacitance retention of 85.6 after 14,000 cycles at 3 A g 1 . Furthermore, the ASC exhibited a high energy density of 54 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 800 W kg 1 . The MXene rGO MoO 3 film produced via vacuum-assisted filtration offers a straightforward and efficient preparation method, providing valuable insights for the development of flexible advanced electrode materials.

title: Hydrothermal synthesis of MoS2 MXene composites for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Jung-Jie Huang, Yu-Wu Wang, Yu-Jie Lin, Yu-Xuan Zhang
abstract: This study explores the use of an MXene framework as a substrate for MoS2 nanomaterials in supercapacitor thin-film electrodes, tackling the issues of reduced specific capacitance and poor energy storage performance caused by MoS2 agglomeration. The results show that integrating MoS2 with the MXene base effectively reduces agglomeration, enhancing structural stability and conductivity. After annealing, the MoS2 phase shifted from a mixed 1 T 2H to a more stable 2H phase, optimizing the composition and increasing crystallinity. Consequently, the specific capacitance of the MoS2 MXene electrode rose from 60.41 to 88.00 F g, representing a 1.46-fold improvement in electrochemical performance. Notably, after 15,000 charge discharge cycles, the electrode retained 100 of its capacitance, demonstrating outstanding cycling stability. Overall, the findings confirm the high electrochemical reversibility and long-term stability of MoS2 MXene composites, positioning them as promising candidates for advanced energy storage applications.
conclusion: This study used an MXene framework to mitigate the restacking and agglomeration of MoS2 in the electrodes of capacitors. Through hydrothermal synthesis, MoS2 was grown on MXene base to create MoS2 MXene heterostructure materials. Ultrasonic spray coating was employed to fabricate MoS2 MXene electrodes, thereby ensuring the uniformity and quality of the materials. The structural advantages of MXene effectively prevented the restacking of MoS2 , which enabled the electrodes to maintain favorable dispersion and high overall capacitive performance. The electrochemical performance and stability of MoS2 MXene were investigated under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios. Among MoS2 MXene electrodes prepared under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios, the electrode prepared under a concentration ratio of 0.04:0.4 M exhibited the optimal electrochemical performance and stability. Therefore, the capacitive performance of MoS2 MXene electrodes prepared under the aforementioned concentration ratio and subjected to different annealing temperatures was examined. Among the MoS2 MXene electrodes annealed at various temperatures, that annealed at 850 C had the optimal performance. At 850 C, MoS2 transitioned from a 1 T 2H mixed phase to a more stable 2H phase; thus, the electrode annealed at this temperature exhibited higher crystallinity than did the electrodes annealed at different temperatures. Moreover, it exhibited the highest specific capacitance among the electrodes. The specific capacitance of the MoS2 MXene electrode annealed at 850 C (88.00 F g) was approximately 1.46 times higher than that of an unannealed MoS2 MXene electrode (60.41 F g). Thus, the MoS2 MXene electrode annealed at 850 C had high charge storage capacity and excellent electrochemical performance. Furthermore, after 15000 charge discharge cycles at a high current density of 20 A g, the capacitance retention of the aforementioned electrode remained 100 , which indicated its exceptional long-term cycling stability, durability, and reliability. In summary, the results of this study confirmed that thermally annealed MoS2 MXene composites are promising high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors. title: High-performance Zn-ion hybrid supercapacitor based on 3D K+-intercalated Ti3C2TX hydrogel cathode
authors: Haiping Wang, Xingyu Wang, Xinmiao Liu, Shuwei Zhang, Shutong Meng, Wenjie Yan, Xin Zhang, Zhansheng Lu, Zenghui Qiu, Haijun Xu, Jiaqi He
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors (ZHSCs) exhibit great potential for energy storage and conversion devices, owing to their inherent safety and cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, the structure of traditional porous carbon cathodes hinders the zinc-ion diffusion kinetics, rendering the energy densities of conventional ZHSCs uncompetitive and severely impeding their practical applications. 2D transition metal carbides nitrides, known as MXenes, exhibit excellent conductivity and abundant surface functional groups, qualifying them as ideal candidates for constructing high-capacity cathodes in high-performance ZHSCs. This study presents the fabrication of a ZHSC utilizing 3D porous K+-intercalated Ti3C2TX-reduced graphene oxide (K+-Ti3C2TX-RGO) hydrogel as cathode, paired with a zinc foil as anode. Upon treatment with KOH solution, Ti3C2TX undergoes K+ ion intercalation into its nanosheets, resulting in partial elimination of terminal -F groups and expansion of the MXene interlayer spacing. Subsequently, large-scale graphene oxide (GO) was employed as a conductive binder to interconnect the intercalated multilayer Ti3C2TX, and a reducing agent was incorporated to facilitate self-assembly into a hydrogel. This approach augmented the accessibility of ions and facilitated their transport within the resultant structure. The ZHSC, fabricated with this composite cathode, synergistically integrates the supercapacitor s high-power density and the battery s high energy density. The results indicate that the ZHSC exhibited excellent electrochemical performance, featuring a high specific capacitance of 253.86 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 and an impressive energy density of 141.03 Wh kg 1 at 999.99 W kg 1. Notably, after 5000 charge-discharge cycles at 10 A g 1, the ZHSC maintained a capacitance retention rate above 87.96 , highlighting its exceptional cycling stability.
conclusion: 4 Conclusion K + intercalation of Ti 3 C 2 T X inhibits the self-stacking of MXene material due to interlayer van der Waals forces, thus enlarging the layer spacing and achieving fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics; and the reduction of the intercalated Ti 3 C 2 T X with GO by ascorbic acid generates a RGO hydrogel in a composite 3D system, which further contributes to the fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics. The use of this material in the cathode for ZHSCs results in excellent electrochemical performance, which feature a high specific capacitance of 253.86 F g 1 at a current density of 1 A g 1 and an impressive energy density of 141.03 Wh kg 1 at 999.99 W kg 1 . Notably, after 5000 charge-discharge cycles at a current density of 10 A g 1 , the ZHSC maintained a capacitance retention rate above 87.96 , highlighting its exceptional cycling stability. Our study provides robust evidence that 3D K + -Ti 3 C 2 T X -RGO integration endows ZHSCs with exceptional electrochemical properties. This finding holds profound significance for advancing the development of ZHSCs. Furthermore, our research findings address the inherent limitations of MXene and offer valuable insights that could inspire novel avenues for exploring the energy storage applications of MXene.

title: Review: 2D MXenes based electrochemical sensors and supercapacitors for biomedical and energy storage applications
authors: Sourav Karmakar, Anuprava Mandal, Naresh Kumar Mani, Rinky Sha
abstract: MXenes, composed of early transition metal carbides and or nitrides, have become one of the most versatile two-dimensional materials. High metallic conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, rich surface functional groups, large specific surface area, good redox capabilities, hydrophilicity, high energy storage ability, layered structure for ion intercalations, and other remarkable properties have made MXenes increasingly popular in a range of scientific applications, including sensors and energy storage. A thorough analysis of the characteristics and synthesis routes of MXenes is presented, highlighting the importance of these approaches in tailoring MXene nanostructures for use in supercapacitors and sensing. The recent advancements in MXene-based electrochemical sensors for the detection of several vital biomolecules, such as glucose, ascorbic acid, uric acid, dopamine, microRNAs, l-methionine, melatonin, cortisol, etc., are fully inspected in this review paper with a focus on sensing performances, including sensitivity, limit of detection, selectivity, dynamic range, stability, linearity, and their viability in real samples. Further, this review highlights various MXenes based electrodes, including pristine MXenes, doped MXene, MXenes carbonaceous nanocomposites, MXenes transition metal oxide composites, MXenes transition metal-dichalcogenides composites for the application of supercapacitors, emphasizing their usefulness in practical applications as well as their capacitive characteristics, including specific capacitance, cyclic stability, energy and power densities, and others. A deeper understanding of how MXenes is attributed to each supercapacitor is provided by discussing basic charge-storage mechanisms. The limitations of the current methods and the future outlooks of MXenes based electrochemical biosensors and MXenes based supercapacitors are also discussed where appropriate.
conclusion: 6 Conclusion future outlook MXenes similar to graphene have recently attracted a significant attention among research communities because of their promising physico-chemical, and electronic characteristics, which position them as a possible substitute for graphene. With a focus on sensing performances, including sensitivity, LOD, selectivity, stability, linearity, dynamic range, and their viability in real samples, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the various methods that MXenes are synthesized as well as the latest advancements in electrochemical biosensors that are designed to detect a variety of biomarkers. The impressive metallic conductivities, vast surface area, diverse composition, and remarkable hydrophilicity make these materials useful for developing electrochemical sensing devices. Consequently, there is a promising outlook for their use as sensitive electrochemical sensors in detecting a wide range of analytes. Although there has been notable advancement, the domain still faces numerous obstacles to overcome for the successful commercialization of MXene-based electrochemical biosensors, which can be outlined as follows: (1) Limited resistance to oxidation: the process of MXenes oxidizing in oxygen-rich solvents. (2) Scalability in synthesis presents challenges, particularly in achieving commercial-scale production. The environmental hazards associated with HF necessitate the exploration of alternative, milder etchants such as LiF HCl. In recent years, less harmful and environmentally friendly etching techniques such as H 3 PO 4 , DES, and TBAOH have been introduced to alleviate the problem. (3) Irregular surface termination and absence of fluorine: it is essential to steer clear of random functionalization of the MXene surface by employing a different approach than the traditional HF-based etching method. Additionally, the presence of fluorine on the MXenes surface hinders their use in biomedical applications and the immobilization of biomarkers. (4) Surface imperfections: the process of delaminating MXene through ultrasonication can lead to the formation of surface imperfections that may alter the distinctive physiochemical properties of MXenes. Moreover, addressing the technological hurdles is crucial for the successful advancement of electrochemical biosensors into commercial applications. The upcoming sensors must prioritize the followings: (1) broadening of sensing devices to encompass a diverse array of biomarkers through simultaneous non-invasive immunoassays, enabling the monitoring of individuals health at the molecular level. (2) the development of secure and dependable biosensing diagnostic platforms that leverage valuable insights from population studies and their correlation to blood-based clinical assays. This area is anticipated to evolve over time with significant advancements in production, processing, electrochemical conversion, and integration. Further, this review highlights the various MXenes based electrodes, including pristine MXenes, doped MXene, MXenes carbonaceous nanocomposites, MXenes transition metal oxide composites, MXenes transition metal-dichalcogenides composites for the application of supercapacitors. The heteroatom doped MXenes and various MXenes composites exhibit better electrochemical performance and much suitable for practical applications due to its high specific surface area, high ionic and electronic conductivity, modified electronic structure, rich of active sites, enhanced inter-planar spacing, better chemical stability, improved operating voltage window, and prevention of the restacking problems of MXene nanosheets. As a result, the modified electrodes offered high specific capacitance, excellent cycling stability, and excellent rate capability. Despite the fact, that MXene-based electrodes showed remarkable progress as an energy storage device for supercapacitor applications they also faced various challenges. Therefore, further research in the field of sustainable energy storage should be done to overcome those challenges. Hereby, some future recommendations for supercapacitor applications are shortlisted. 1. To enhance the electrochemical performance of pristine-MXenes, the surface chemistry of MXenes should be modified using appropriate synthesis process. 2. Researchers should focus on the novel composite based MXenes to increase the energy density with high power density and prevent the restacking problem of MXene nanosheets and the electrodes should be engineered with defects and heteroatom doping to enhance the electrochemical performances. 3. To explore the various properties of MXenes researchers should focus on the combined experimental and theoretical studies. 4. Exploration of non-Ti-based MXenes, double-M MXenes, and double-X MXenes for the application of supercapacitors are also highly demanded. 5. For better cycling stability, the degradation of material properties at the time of cycling should be carefully observed by material characterization techniques like in-situ XRD and Raman studies and should find out the root cause of capacitance degradation. Therefore, we can get an idea about the changes of the material properties during cycling and it can be resolved by modifying the synthesis techniques and other modifications. 6. MXenes show promising performance in aqueous electrolytes but the limited potential window for aqueous electrolyte limits the electrode to achieve high energy density and the leakage of aqueous electrolyte restrict the practical applications of the devices. Therefore, the use of non-aqueous electrolytes and solid electrolytes are preferable. Overall, the rigorous research in this area will enable 2D MXenes to overcome these obstacles for the practical applications. Therefore, this review is anticipated to have a significant influence on the investigation and development of 2D MXenes-based electrochemical sensors for use in supercapacitors and biomedical applications.

title: Synthesis and fabrication of MXene copper selenide composite for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: M. Manikandan, M. Muthulakshmi, Seyadu Abuthahir, E. Papanasam, Dr Deepak Dubal, Sajid Ali Ansari, E. Manikandan

A composite material with improved ion transport, increased conductivity, superior cyclic stability and specific capacitance is produced when MXene is incorporated into a CuSe matrix. title: Recent advances in MXene-polymer composites for high performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Sanam Bashir, Lala Gurbanova, Ibrahim A. Shaaban, Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Md Rezaul Karim, Syed Shoaib Ahmad Shah, Muhammad Altaf Nazir
abstract: MXene conducting polymers are excellent electrode materials that have drawn a great deal of scientific focus for energy storage applications. When these two distinct material types, MXene and polymers are combined, the flaws that arise from their use as electrode materials alone can be resolved. MXene conducting polymer composites show promise as improved electrode materials because of their superior mechanical characteristics, mass load, flexibility, specific surface area, and theoretical capacity. Numerous instances of employing conducting polymers with MXene as electrodes are detailed in order to further highlight the modifications caused by these composites. The latest developments in the study of conducting polymer composites and MXene-based supercapacitors (SC) are generally covered in this review, covering various properties of MXene and MXene-polymers composites, electrode materials, materials preparation, and the two types of supercapacitors: symmetrical (SSC) and asymmetrical (ASC). Understanding the utilizing of composites of MXene and conducting polymers in SC research is the purpose of this work, which also offers recommendations for additional study of these intriguing materials.
conclusion: 7 Conclusion and outlook Supercapacitors have made extensive use of conducting polymers because of their high theoretical capacity, cheap access to raw ingredients, inexpensive preparation costs, straightforward synthesis techniques, etc. In barely 10 years, MXene has generated a significant curiosity from scholars due to its exceptional conductivity comparable to that of metal and enormous graphene-like usable ion surface area. This paper examines the latest achievements in the research of MXene conducting polymer composites and supercapacitors are conducted on electrode materials, composite material manufacture, SSCs, and ASCs. MXene and conducting polymers has been the subject of much research, but some obstacles still stand in the way of their widespread use. From the standpoint of material preparation, conductive polymers need careful control over the duration of polymerization and the design of preparation schemes since they have distinct morphologies and are prone to agglomeration. Strong, corrosive acids such concentrated HCl and HF are used to etch MXene compounds. It is clear from the papers previously cited in the text that MXene produced using various etching techniques differs in size, shape, and surface functional groups. More convenient and mild etching techniques must be investigated for the mass synthesis of MXene. Furthermore, the MXene precursor s MAX phase use rate is rather low, therefore when looking into more easy and gentle etching technique, it s important to think about ways to increase the MAX phase s utilization rate. From the standpoint of material storage, low temperature can lessen MXene s oxidation, but they cannot stop converting MXene to TiO 2 containing molecules of water and oxygen. The researchers used end-group protection to lessen the interaction between oxygen and water molecules and functional groups on the surface of MXene to address the problem of improved MXene material utilization. For instance, Wu et al. [ 262 ] used sodium citrate for MXene s end-group protection; the outcomes shown that the end-base protection significantly extended MXene s storage period. However, MXene s storage mechanism remains a challenging issue that prevents its widespread use. From the perspective of electrode material use, MXene is highly susceptible to self-stacking because, when the transition metal is removed away, there is no support material left. When charging and discharging, conducting polymers swell, this impairs their performance in electrochemistry. Along with fixing the problems of conducting polymer expansion when charging and discharging and MXene self-accumulation, the successful union of conductive polymers with MXene confers advantageous properties on the electrode material, such as enhanced stability and more adjustable usage conditions (such as pH and temperature). Additionally, MXene has been progressively employed in numerous applications since its beginnings, such as adsorption, sensors, batteries, SCs, and electromagnetic shielding. Nonetheless, MXenes component parts and surface functional groups differ, making them varied. The structure, chemistry, and form of conducting polymers also differ. Numerous elements of MXene s characteristics are yet unknown, and its potential has not been completely utilized. Along with the need to address the previously outlined outstanding concerns, theoretical simulation calculations and experiments may be combined in the future. In addition to increasing research efficiency and cutting down on needless exploration time, an efficient computer system should be able to create composite materials with various topologies based on various application scenarios. Because of its exceptional and distinctive qualities, MXene is anticipated to be used in a wider range of research domains as its study progresses. MXene conducting polymer composites have great potential in high-performing supercapacitors as a result of their synergic properties i.e. high conductivity of MXene and pseudocapacitance of polymers. However, some challenges of MXene oxidation, polymer swelling, restacking, and harsh etching techniques constrain real world application. Future work should entail the development of green, scalable etching processes, improvements on the stability of MXene through surface passivation, and the utilization of the control of morphology in polymerization. Counteracting self-stacking and agglomeration, on the one hand, with the help of 3D architectures and, on the other hand, with the spacer materials, is essential. Combination of computational modeling and machine learning could advance the design of optimized composites design. Besides, in situ characterization and long-term device evaluation will be critical in transforming material-level progress to real energy storage systems. By using theoretical, experimental, and engineering methodologies, it is possible to tune these composites for flexible, effective, and scalable supercapacitor applications. The main challenge is that numerous prior documented attempts have relied on polymer materials and MXene, as well as their composites with MOFs, phosphates, sulphides, oxides, and other chemicals. When researching ESDs for supercapacitor applications, researchers encounter a significant obstacle due to the limited availability of MXene polymer material. Therefore, combining battery-grade polymers will boost the energy and power density of the devices. Furthermore, the composite of polymer-based materials with MXene (because to its remarkable hydrophilicity) would enhance the device s performance and spark the next generation s curiosity about ESDs, as polymer-based materials exhibit extraordinary EIS performance. Chemical and thermodynamic stability are also important considerations for the materials being used. MXene is susceptible to oxidation when exposed to H 2 O and O 2 . Therefore, a detailed investigation into the preparation or regulation of MXene to ensure long-term stability is necessary. While sodium ascorbate has been employed as an antioxidant, there is an urgent need for a more efficient way to increase MXene s resistance to oxidation. Additionally, for applications requiring temperatures greater than room temperature, it is necessary to design new polymer capacitors based on MXene. The current review discussed the various methods of producing MXene and its mechanical, electrical, thermal, optical, magnetic, dielectric, structural, compositional, and functional characteristics. It also highlighted recent advancements in the development of MXene and polymer-based composites-based high-performance supercapacitor devices. The mechanical, electrical, and thermal characteristics of MXene-polymer composites are further highlighted. Last but not least, the development and uses of the next-generation SCs take into account the difficulties and potential future developments associated with MXene polymer nanocomposites. In numerous applications, MXene polymer nanocomposites have shown their significant latent potential. Therefore, we hope that our analysis would help researchers identify suitable composite energy storage devices based on MXene and polymers to enhance desirable qualities. In order to create MXene polymer composites with remarkable and all-encompassing electrochemical performance, future researchers will also find this review helpful as they continue to improve MXene stripping and dispersion techniques.

title: Recent advance in the construction of 3D porous structure Ti3C2Tx MXene and their multi-functional applications
authors: Wenke Hao, Sijia Ren, Xiaodong Wu, Xiaodong Shen, Sheng Cui
abstract: MXene, a new two-dimensional nanomaterial, has attracted much attention due to its hydrophilicity, excellent electrical conductivity, stability, electrochemical property, etc. We have given a brief introduction to the preparation of MXene nanosheets, as well as the 1D and 2D MXene-based materials with their applications. However, the spontaneous aggregation and re-stacking of nanosheets in 1D and 2D MXene due to hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces are not beneficial to the industrialization applications, and therefore, the construction of 3D porous structures is an effective way to solve this issue. However, the small transverse dimensions and weak mechanical properties of MXene itself do not allow for the spontaneous formation of strong, stable, and self-supportable 3D porous structure. Therefore, combining MXene with other materials, such as carbon-based materials, metal oxides, spinel, polymers, metal-based nanoparticles, have been considered as the most effective method for the preparation of 3D MXene-based porous structure. Thus, in this review, we have illustrated the current construction techniques of 3D porous Ti3C2Tx MXene including template method, self-assembly method and 3D printing method, etc. The wide applications of 3D MXene in supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding, seawater desalination, piezoresistive sensors and catalysis via microstructures structures regulation, are also summarized in this work. Finally, the prospects regarding the 3D MXene-based composites with strong mechanical property, pore structures regulation, cost-effective synthesis route and the new applications fields are proposed. This work will help to develop a more exquisite design of 3D MXene-based materials for their future commercial applications.
conclusion: 4 Summary and outlook This review has summarized the definition and preparation of MXene-based fibers whiskers and films nanosheets, and emphasized on the different kinds of and MXene-based 3D macro aggregations for wide applications including supercapacitors, piezoresistive sensors, electromagnetic shielding, microwave absorption, seawater desalination and catalysis attributed to their rapid electron transfer rate, large specific surface area, contactable active sites, and stable porous channels. Many achievements have been made during the past few years in the construction of different kinds of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations using carbon-based materials, metal oxides, spinel, polymers, metal-based nanoparticles, etc., as the second phase, yet challenges and opportunities remain as follows: (1) Further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. Many MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been obtained so far, however, the weak interaction of the electrostatic interaction, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces between MXene nanosheets and the other components, have induced the weak mechanical performance, which can be only used in the laboratory scale and have limited their further industrialization applications. Therefore, we should try to effectively control the abundant functional groups on the surface of MXene via the green chemical synthesis route, therefore to improve the interaction strength between the MXene and other components via the strong intermolecular forces and covalent bond, etc. Furthermore, the design of structures, such as the oriented structure and recrystallization texture, should be attracted more attention for the further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the 3D porous material, therefore to obtain more robust and stronger MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. (2) Construction of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations with controllable pore structures. MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been frequently prepared by sacrificial template and lyophilization methods, but the pore sizes prepared by these methods are mostly in the range of several tens of micrometers, therefore have limited their specific surface area and their wide applications as supercapacitor, catalysts, and adsorbents. Therefore, the design of controllable pore structures is in highly demand, and the control of building sub-micron-level structures should be explored by combining multiscale theoretical calculations via density functional theory, molecular dynamics, and mesoscopic dynamics, as well as the in-situ characterization techniques such as the in-situ FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), TEM (Transmission Electron Microscope), XAS (X-ray Absorption Spectra), Raman (Raman spectra), etc to further achieve precise control of the pore structures. (3) Decrease the fabrication cost and explore more applications of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. As is reported in this work, the unique properties of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have led to their different application in certain fields, such as supercapacitors, electromagnetic interference shielding, pressure sensors, seawater desalination, and catalysis. However, industrial applications of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations are still in their infancy due to the single and expensive fabrication route of the MXene nanosheets, therefore, the cost-effective fabrication technique for MXene nanosheets with high performance should be developed in further study. In addition, the excellent thermal, electric, and mechanical properties of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations should be expanded to many other fields in the future, such as thermoelectric material, superconducting material, solar cell, biocompatibility, electrocommunication, anti-microbico, etc.

title: FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4 core-shell nanospheres intercalating into Ti3C2Tx for high-performance all-solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Na Chen, Guo-Tao Xiang, Qi Sun, Jia-Lei Xu, Bin Lu, Wen-Cheng Hu, Yong-Da Hu, Jin-Ju Chen
abstract: Electrode materials with high electrochemical activity and outstanding stability is of great significance to improve the performance of supercapacitors. A composite material comprised of core-shell FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4 nanospheres and MXene nanosheets was synthesized through solvothermal combined with self-assembly. The FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4-MXene hybrids as electrode materials exhibit a high specific capacitance of 1090.6 F g 1 at 1 A g 1. All-solid-state supercapacitor using FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4-MXene as the positive electrode possesses a high energy density of 49.8 Wh kg 1 at 800 W kg 1and great cycle life with 87.85 retention over 20,000 cycles at 1 A g 1. The synergistic effect of FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4 and MXene is the main reason for the exceptional electrochemical performance. FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4 anchored to MXene prevents the restacking of MXene, while MXene provides a conductive network for accelerating carrier transfer and a skeleton for preventing FeCo2O4 FeCo2S4 from collapsing during long-term cycling. In view of the above excellent performance, this study provides a feasible idea for future research on high-performance supercapacitors.
conclusion: In summary, core-shell FeCo2 O4 FeCo2 S4 nanospheres were anchored into lamellar MXene nanosheets by solvothermal combined with a self-assembly method. The FeCo2 O4 FeCo2 S4 -MXene electrode benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two materials exhibits a promising energy storage capacity of 1090.6 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 . Furthermore, All-solid-state FeCo2 O4 FeCo2 S4 -MXene AC asymmetric supercapacitor shows a high energy density of 49.8 Wh kg 1 at 800 W kg 1 and an outstanding cycle stability of 87.85 after 20000 charge discharge cycles. These results demonstrate the enormous potential of FeCo2 O4 FeCo2 S4 -MXene in practical supercapacitors.

title: High-rate electrospun Ti3C2Tx MXene carbon nanofiber electrodes for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Hyewon Hwang, Segi Byun, Seoyeon Yuk, Seulgi Kim, Sung Ho Song, Dongju Lee
abstract: Increasing the capacitance and rate performance of the carbon-based electrodes used in flexible supercapacitors remains a key challenge for commercial viability. To meet these requirements, free-standing Ti3C2Tx MXene carbon nanofiber (CNF) electrodes were prepared by electrospinning of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and carbonization for application as flexible supercapacitor electrodes. The effects of Ti3C2Tx MXene size on fiber formation and electrochemical performance were investigated. Ti3C2Tx MXene CNF electrodes exhibited a specific capacitance of 90 F g at a fast scan rate of 300 mV s, which is almost 2.3 times higher than that of a pure PAN-derived CNF (38 F g at 300 mV s), while showing similar capacitance values of around 120 F g at the slow scan rate of 2 mV s. Due to the high degree of mechanical flexibility of CNFs, MXene CNF based flexible supercapacitors also demonstrate long-term cycling stability (98 retention after 10 K charge-discharge cycles), and outstanding flexibility in dynamic bend tests. These results suggest that the MXene CNFs have great potential for applications in flexible and versatile electronic devices.
conclusion: 4 Conclusion In summary, free-standing Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene CNF electrodes with various MXene sizes were prepared by electrospinning for use in flexible supercapacitors. This versatile and simple technique provided a large surface area and aligned Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets for good dispersion in the fibers. These electrodes demonstrated good gravimetric capacitance up to 120 F g at 2 mV s, and maintained a higher capacitance value of 90 F g at 300 mV s in comparison to pure CNF electrodes. They also exhibited outstanding flexibility, as demonstrated by dynamic bending tests. Based on these results, MXene-based nanofibers have great potential for applications in flexible and versatile electronic devices beyond energy storage, including electrocatalysis, absorption, and filtration.

title: Synergistically boosting the performance of asymmetric supercapacitors: in-situ construction of NiCo2S4 on amino-functionalized and Zn2+-predoped multilayer MXene
authors: Min Lu, Mingwu Chen, Xiaohui Xu, Xinyan Wang, Wenxiao Zhang, Xinyu Li
abstract: MXene s inherent tendency to aggregate and agglomerate poses critical challenges for its application in energy storage. This phenomenon results in reduced interlayer spacing, a decline in the number of active sites, diminished ion adsorption capacity, and obstructed ion transport pathways, all of which severely limit its practical utility. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel multi-dimensional performance optimization strategy for supercapacitor composite electrode materials. Amino functional groups were first adsorbed onto the surface of multilayer Ti-based MXene as a means of modification, giving rise to amino-MXene (N-MX). Subsequently, Zn2+ ions were intercalated into N-MX to fabricate Zn-amino-MXene (Zn-N-MX), which served as a substrate. Upon this, transition metal nickel cobalt based sulfides were grown in situ and progressively nucleated, culminating in the synthesis of Zn-N-MX NiCo2S4 composites (Zn-N-MX NCS). The introduction of amino functional groups effectively reshapes the chemical surroundings on the surface of MXene and reduces the steric hindrance of Zn2+ insertion. At the same time, the coordination bond formed by the amino group and the metal ion further promotes the stable anchoring and embedding of Zn2+ ions in the interlayer, as if opening up a fast lane for their embedding. In addition, the homogeneous dispersion of NiCo2S4 nanoparticles in the MXene layer provides a complementary quick channel for ion migration, thus boosting the comprehensive electrochemical properties of Zn-N-MX NCS. The composite manifests a conspicuously enhanced electrochemical performance of 1546.76 F g 1 at 1 A g 1. After Zn-N-MX NCS was integrated into an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) Zn-N-MX NCS AC, it exhibits a high energy density of 53.3 Wh kg 1 at 800 W kg 1.
conclusion: Based on a two-step modification strategy, the Zn-N-MX was designed to solve the problems of low conductivity and reduced electron transport capacity caused by surface functionalization and agglomeration of multilayer MXene. Zn-N-MX NCS was further synthesized. The optimized electrode has a high specific capacitance of 1546.76 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 , which is significantly better than MX NCS (1311.11 F g 1 ). The fabricated Zn1.0 -N-MX NCS AC ASC demonstrates remarkable electrochemical performance. It exhibits a high specific capacitance of 150 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 . Regarding its cycle stability, it retains 87.5 of its initial capacitance after 5000 cycles. Moreover, at a power density of 800 W kg 1 , a high energy density of 53.3 Wh kg 1 is achieved. The multi-dimensional control strategy for the structure and electrical properties of MXene, proposed in this study, effectively promotes the practical application of supercapacitors. title: Hybrid microsupercapacitors based on Ti3C2Tx MXene and covalent organic frameworks
authors: Yusuf Khan, Vinayak S. Kale, Jehad K. El-Demellawi, Yongjiu Lei, Wenli Zhao, Sharath Kandambeth, Prakash T. Parvatkar, Osama Shekhah, Mohamed Eddaoudi, Husam N. Alshareef
abstract: The growing demand for emerging electronic applications, including energy storage, sensors, and portable devices, has created a pressing need to develop miniaturized flexible energy storage components with convenient device architecture. Here, we report an in-plane hybrid micro-supercapacitor made of covalent organic frameworks and Ti3C2Tx MXene as positive and negative electrodes, respectively. The devices utilize three-dimensional laser-scribed graphene (LSG) as a current collector for both electrodes using a CO2-laser-based technique due to its good resolution for in-plane device fabrication, and high porosity of LSG that can facilitate better rate performance. title: In situ growth of oxometallate-based coordination polymer decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene with enhanced water-assisted proton channels for flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor
authors: Ying Huang, Shuai Zhang, Jiaming Wang, Xiaopeng Han, Xu Sun
abstract: As promising electrode material contender for supercapacitors, MXene has high conductivity, abundant surface functional groups, and large surface area. However, the self-restacking of MXene leads to poor ion-accessible surface area and restricted ion transport routes. Water-assisted proton channels contained by Polyoxometallate-based coordination polymer (POMCP) can improve the efficiency of ion transport between MXene layers, which is conducive to enhancing the storage capacity and rate performance. Herein, [PW12O40] [Cu6O(TZI)3(H2O)6]4 OH 31H2O (CuCP) decorated Ti3C2Tx (CuCP MX) was synthesized by in-situ hydrothermal method. Attribute to the extended interlayer space and enhanced ion transport efficiency, CuCP MX exhibits excellent electrochemical energy storage properties. It is worth revealing that when assembling into an all-solid-state supercapacitor device (SC), excellent specific capacitance (380 mF cm2) and energy density (68.4 μWh cm2 at 540 μW cm2) were exhibited. CuCP MX is a considerable electrode material for supercapacitors for flexible electronic devices.
conclusion: This work reports a method for the in-situ growth of CuCP on the surface of MXene to improve the electrochemical performance of MXene. The newly introduced electrochemical activity, extended interlayer space, and functionalized interlayer ion transport channels of CuCP contribute to enhanced capacitance performance, rate performance, and stability.
