title: The surface functional modification of Ti3C2Tx MXene by phosphorus doping and its application in quasi-solid state flexible supercapacitor
authors: Xiaochun Wei, Man Cai, Fulin Yuan, Dan Lu, Cong Li, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
abstract: The surface modification of MXene by heterogeneous atoms shows great potential in improving the charge storage capacity of MXene. Herein, a strategy of rapid in-situ phosphorus doping at low temperature is demonstrated for preparing functionalized Ti3C2Tx MXene (Ti3C2Tx-P) using sodium hypophosphate as phosphorus source. The phosphorus doping can increase the layer spacing of Ti3C2Tx and yield PO and PC bonds in Ti3C2Tx, resulting in more rapid paths for the migration of electrolyte ions into electrode and more active sites for pseudocapacitance effects. As flexible electrode of supercapacitor, the specific capacitance of Ti3C2Tx-P reaches as high as 476.9F g 1 (745.4F cm 3), which is far larger than that of the raw Ti3C2Tx (344.4F g 1, 438.5F cm 3). In addition, a flexible quasi-solid supercapacitor device assembled by Ti3C2Tx-P film shows high specific capacitance of 103F g 1 at 5 mV s 1. When the power density is 250 W kg 1 and 10000 W kg 1, the corresponding energy density reaches 15.8 Wh kg 1 and 6.1 Wh kg 1, respectively. Therefore, our work not only reveals the role of P atom doping in improving the structure, composition and electrochemical performance of Ti3C2Tx, but provides a method for surface modification and functionalization of MXene materials.
conclusion: In summary, we reported a simple preparation method of P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, in which sodium hypophosphate was used as a phosphorus source and phosphorus was doped by the heat treatment. The P-doping level is in the range 0.9 1.11 at by this method. After heat treatment, the expansion of layer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene promotes the rapid transport and diffusion of electrolyte ions into electrode interface. At the same time, the d-spacing of MXene is further expanded because the introduction of P atoms increases the adsorption effect. The P O and P C bonds generated provide more active sites, resulting in the enhanced energy storage performance of the electrode. As expected, the specific capacitance of P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene is as high as 476.9F g 1 , far larger than that of raw Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Furthermore, the quasi-solid flexible supercapacitor assembled by Ti3 C2 Tx -P-3h film electrode can reach high energy density of 15.8 Wh kg 1 at power density of 250 W kg 1 . These results demonstrate that P doping plays an important role in improving the structure, composition and electrochemical performance of MXene materials. This work also provides a new way to achieve high specific capacitance and excellent retention performance of MXene electrodes. title: 2,6-Diaminoanthraquinone modified MXene (Ti3C2Tx) graphene as the negative electrode materials for ionic liquid-based asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Li Sun, Lujia Chai, Liangqi Jing, Yujuan Chen, Kelei Zhuo, Jianji Wang
abstract: Due to insufficient energy density, supercapacitors (SCs) with preeminent-power and long cycle stability cannot be implemented in some practical applications. Exploring hybrid materials with redox activity to emerge high specific capacitance in ionic liquid (IL) electrolytes can solve this problem. Herein, we report a redox-organic molecule 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (DAAQ) modified MXene (Ti3C2Tx) Graphene (DAAQ-M G) composite material. With the assist of graphene oxide (GO), MXene and graphene fabricate a three-dimensional (3D) interconnected structure as a conductive framework, which inhibits self-stacking of MXene monolayers and ensures high electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, DAAQ is loaded onto the M G framework through covalent non-covalent functionalization. The DAAQ as a spacer effectively enlarges the interlayer spacing of MXene nanosheets, and meanwhile produces reversible redox reactions during charge discharge processes to provide additional Faradaic contribution to capacity. Therefore, the specific capacitance (capacity) of the DAAQ-M G as the negative electrode material reaches to 226 F g 1 (306 C g 1) at 1 A g 1 in 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EmimBF4) electrolyte. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) is assembled using DAAQ-M G as the negative electrode and self-prepared organic molecule hydroquinone modified reduced graphene oxide (HQ-RGO) material as the positive electrode, with a high energy density of 43 Wh kg 1 at high power density of 1669 W kg 1. The ASC can maintain 80 of initial specific capacitance after 9000 cycles. This research can provide better support to develop advanced organic molecules-modified MXene composite materials for ionic liquid-based SCs.
conclusion: In summary, DAAQ-modified MXene and graphene composites (DAAQ-M G-y ) were successfully fabricated through covalent and non-covalent interactions. DAAQ-M G-40 as the negative electrode exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 226 F g 1 at a current density of 1 A g 1 in EmimBF4 electrolyte, which is mainly due to the high electronic conductivity and added Faradaic contribution. Anchored-DAAQ with redox activity can undergo fast reversible Faradaic reactions to contribute capacity. At the mass-balancing mass-ratio of the negative and positive electrodes, the HQ-RGO-360 DAAQ-M G-40 ASC device delivered a high energy density of 43 Wh kg 1 with an excellent cycle stability. MXene-based composites modified by organic molecules would provide alternative electrode materials for developing excellent energy storage devices. title: Enhancing the ion accessibility of Ti3C2Tx MXene films by femtosecond laser ablation towards high-rate supercapacitors
authors: Xianhong Zheng
abstract: MXenes have attracted tremendous attention in the area of electrochemical energy-storage devices owing to their high electrical conductivity, pseudocapacitance and two-dimensional lamellar structure. Nevertheless, MXene flakes intrinsically tend to lie flat and restack, resulting in highly tortuous ion transport pathways and inferior ion accessibility. Herein, we develop a femtosecond laser ablation strategy to fabricate flexible and high-performance MXene ribbon supercapacitor electrodes. The fabricated MXene ribbons have porous edges with exposed continuous lamellar channels, which shortens the H+ transport pathways, impregnates with sufficient electrolyte, benefits for H+ intercalation and ion storage. The resultant MXene ribbons exhibit high specific capacitance (1308.3 mF cm2), good rate capability and long cycling life (95 capacitance retention and 92 coulombic efficiency after 30,000 cycles). This work provides a new strategy for the rational structure design of high-rate MXene-based supercapacitor electrodes and lays the foundation for the next generation high-performance energy storage devices.
conclusion: In summary, we developed a femtosecond laser ablation strategy for fabricating highly flexible MXene ribbons towards the high-rate supercapacitors. The fabricated MXene ribbons demonstrated good dimension evenness and porous edge structure with exposed lamellar MXene channels. In addition, the MXene ribbons had high specific capacitance of 1308.3 mF cm2 and good rate capability. Moreover, MXene ribbons showed good cycling performance, and there were a 95 capacitance retention and 92 coulombic efficiency after 30,000 GCD cycles. The good electrochemical performance of MXene ribbons was attributed to the synergetic effects between the femtosecond laser ablation induced high specific surface and edge effects. Especially, ribbons edges with continuous MXene flake channels shortened the H+ transport pathways and impregnated with sufficient electrolyte and H+ intercalation. To the best of our knowledge, the electrochemical performance of MXene ribbons exceeds that of most MXene-based supercapacitors. This work provides a new approach for improving the electrochemical performance of MXene-based electrodes, and lays the foundation for the development of high-performance energy storage devices. title: 2D 3D Ti3C2Tx HCl etched Ni-Mn Prussian blue analogue nanocomposite as advanced electrode material for flexible solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Selvadhas Nirmala Kanimozhi, Abdullah Mohammed Alswieleh, Andrea Sorrentino, Jegadesan Subbiah, Anandan Sambandam
abstract: Since their discovery in 2011, MXenes, derived from their parent MAX phases, have garnered immense attention in the domain of energy storage due to their exceptional attributes. However, their performance is often hindered by nanosheet restacking, which limits stability and ion diffusion. To address this challenge, we propose a novel 2D 3D nanocomposite comprising Ti3C2Tx MXene and a 3D Prussian blue analogue (Ni-Mn PBA). The integration of Ni-Mn PBA mitigates the restacking of MXene nanosheets, enhancing electrode stability, while Ti3C2Tx serves as a highly conductive substrate, facilitating efficient ion transport. This synergistic interaction results in superior electrochemical performance. Herein, we report the synthesis of Ti3C2Tx Ni-Mn PBA via chemical etching, which partially modifies the PBA structure to expose internal surfaces and promote ion diffusion through its open framework. The 2D 3D nanocomposite exhibits a specific capacitance of 316 F g at a current density of 5 mA cm2, surpassing the performance of pristine Ti3C2Tx and Ni-Mn PBA. When assembled into an asymmetric supercapacitor, the device achieves an energy density of 44 Wh kg and a power density of 2640 W kg, demonstrating its practical application by powering a multifunctional display for nearly 2 min. Additionally, a solid-state supercapacitor employing an ionic liquid-based gel electrolyte (PVA KOH EMP-TFSI) was developed, extending the operating voltage to 1.7 V and further enhancing the energy density of the device. This study highlights the potential of Ti3C2 Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposites as advanced materials for next-generation flexible energy storage systems.
conclusion: This study presents the successful design and application of a novel 2D 3D nanocomposite, Ti3 C2 Ni-Mn PBA, which effectively addresses some of the key challenges associated with MXenes in energy storage applications. By employing a straightforward fabrication method involving the etching of the Ni-Mn PBA surface, the material was seamlessly anchored onto the conductive Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, resulting in a nanocomposite with significantly enhanced electrochemical performance. The Ti3 C2 Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite achieved a high specific capacitance of 900 F g, outperforming its individual components and demonstrating its ability to compete with leading nanomaterials in the field. When incorporated into a two-electrode asymmetric supercapacitor, the device delivered a remarkable energy density of 44 Wh kg and a power density of 2640 W kg. Additionally, it successfully powered a multifunctional display for approximately 2 min, showcasing its practical utility in real-world applications. An innovative aspect of this work lies in the development of a flexible, binder-free electrode coupled with an ionic liquid-based gel electrolyte (PVA KOH EMP-TFSI). This design provides the device with enhanced mechanical stability, excellent ionic conductivity, and extended durability, paving the way for its integration into wearable and portable electronics, areas of rapidly growing interest. The robust device architecture maintained an outstanding 100 capacitance retention and a 75 coulombic efficiency over 1000 charge-discharge cycles, highlighting its reliability for long-term use. Moreover, the unique synergy between the 2D structure of Ti3 C2 Tx and the 3D open framework of Ni-Mn PBA-augmented by etched surface voids-facilitates rapid ion transport, reduced polarization, and improved charge transfer kinetics. This hybrid approach not only enhances the material s energy storage capacity but also contributes to its exceptional rate capability and reversibility. In light of these findings, the Ti3 C2 Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite represents a significant step forward in the development of high-performance, sustainable energy storage solutions. Future investigations should focus on further optimizing the material s synthesis, exploring its behaviour with other electrolytes, and scaling its production to meet industrial demands. title: Rationally constructed CeO2 Ti3C2Tx-MXene heterostructure for rapid and efficient visible light photocatalytic activity and enhanced supercapacitor performance
authors: Nagaraju Macherla, Govinda Dharmana, Manjula Nerella, Thirumala Rao Gurugubelli, Ravindranadh Koutavarapu, Jaesool Shim
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXene (MX) benefits from substantial surface area, higher electric conductivity, and abundant surface terminations that can be tightly coupled with other materials, and has found broad application prospects in energy storage and photocatalysis. By this, CeO2 nanospheres were rationally compounded with MX to obtain nanocomposites (NCs) (CeO2 MX1, CeO2 MX3, CeO2 MX5, and CeO2 MX7) via a facile one-step solvothermal method. X-ray diffraction examination discloses the cubic structure of CeO2, and shrinkage in average crystallite size is noticed up to 5 of MX. Field emission scanning electron microscopy images show uniform CeO2 nanospheres decorated on MX 2D matrix, and particle size distribution results are well aligned with crystallite size trends. Optical absorption divulges a progressive red shift in the absorption edge with increasing MX content, demonstrating enhanced light harvesting and effective charge migration through the heterojunction formed at the CeO2 MX interface. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy studies indicate a smaller charge transfer resistance for CeO2 MX5, highlighting interfacial conductivity and rapid charge transfer characteristics. Consequently, CeO2 MX5 attains a robust photocatalytic tetracycline (TC) degradation surpassing pristine CeO2 and other CeO2 MX NCs. As a supercapacitor electrode, CeO2 MX5 delivers a specific capacitance of 522 F g 1 at 0.5 A g 1 and retains 92 of its initial capacitance after 10000 GCD cycles. This work underscores the effective integration of CeO2 with 2D MX to achieve a versatile platform for environmental remediation and energy storage applications.
conclusion: 4 Conclusions In summary, CeO 2 nanospheres were successfully compounded with Ti 3 C 2 MXene via solvothermal method. A smaller crystallite size is noticed from XRD for CeO 2 MX5 resulted in reduced particle size of CeO 2 nanospheres ( 87 nm) which were uniformly dispersed over 2D nanosheets of MX. Consequently, a larger specific surface area is realized for CeO 2 MX5 (114.20 m 2 g 1 ) with abundant mesoporosity. XPS surface analysis designates the dual oxidation states (Ce 4+ and Ce 3+ ) of Ceria owing to the rich abundance of reactive oxygen species. Optical study describes the reduced bandgap trend (red-shift) of composites with increasing MX and lower charge transfer resistance is obtained for CeO 2 MX5. Improved TC photodegradation efficiency (96.05 in 120 min) of the optimized composite was due to enhanced charge separation and nano-phased heterostructure. Holes and superoxide ions play a vibrant role in the degradation mechanism and the high stability of the optimized composite even after three consecutive cycles. The significant enhancement is electrochemical activity is realized by achieving enhanced specific capacitance (522 F g 1 at 0.5 A g 1 ) along with a capacitance retention of 92.01 after 5000 cycles. Based on the above merits, the prepared heterostructure was found to be an efficient photocatalyst for degrading TC pollutant from water bodies upon light irradiation and Supercapacitor.

title: Synergistic Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dot nanosheet Hybrid: Elevating supercapacitor performance
authors: Bheem Kumar, Avinash Rundla, Priyanka, Mahaveer Singh, Divya Rani, Pushpendra Kumar, Kedar Singh
abstract: Supercapacitors are promising energy storage devices, offering a unique combination of high energy and power densities. This study systematically investigated the synergistic effect of a Ti3C2Tx-MXene quantum dot (MQD) nanosheet hybrid on supercapacitor performance. Ti3C2Tx MQDs are synthesized through a two-step process: first, Ti3C2Tx MXene 2D sheets are prepared via acidic etching of precursor materials. A combined hydrothermal (water-based) and solvothermal (ethanol-based) treatment at 150 C reduces the sheet size, producing MQDs. The electrochemical performance of the MQD nanosheet hybrid was evaluated via a three-electrode configuration with 1 M H2SO4 as the electrolyte. Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) tests at current densities ranging from 1 to 5 Ag-1 revealed a significant improvement in the specific capacitance under all tested conditions. Similarly, CV at scan rates of 10 200 mVs 1 demonstrated an enhanced charge storage capability and superior rate performance, which was attributed to the synergistic effects of the MQDs. EIS confirmed the reduced charge-transfer resistance and excellent capacitive behavior across a wide frequency range. The enhancement in the results is due to the high surface area, remarkable electrical conductivity, and abundant electrochemically active sites of the MQDs. This study highlights the potential of Ti3C2Tx MQD nanosheet hybrids as high-performance materials for next-generation supercapacitors, paving the way for their integration into advanced energy storage systems.
conclusion: This study demonstrates the successful synthesis and characterization of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx , Water Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol Ti3 C2 Tx , highlighting their synergistic improvements in electrochemical performance. Ti3 C2 Tx was synthesized via the etching of MAX-phase precursors in an acidic solution to remove the Al layer, forming a combination of nanosheets and MQDs that enhance the surface area for charge and ion transport. The materials were characterized via XRD for their crystal structure, FTIR for their functional groups, TEM for their morphological analysis, and UV vis and PL spectroscopy for their optical properties. Electrochemical studies were performed in a three-electrode system with 1 M H2 SO4 as the electrolyte, with the materials coated on nickel foil used as working electrodes. CV, GCD, and EIS analyses demonstrated significant enhancements in the specific capacitance and charge transfer properties of Water Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol Ti3 C2 Tx compared with those of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . Both materials exhibited higher specific capacitances across varying current densities (1 5 Ag-1 ) and scan rates (10-200 mVs 1 ). The EIS results further revealed a reduced Rct and Rs in Water Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol Ti3 C2 Tx , indicating superior electrochemical kinetics. These findings underscore the potential of functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx materials for advanced energy storage applications. title: Cu1.5Mn1.5O4 hollow sphere decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene for flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor and electromagnetic wave absorber
authors: Shuai Zhang, Ying Huang, Jiaming Wang, Xiaopeng Han, Guozheng Zhang, Xu Sun
abstract: Flexible energy storage systems and electromagnetic pollution have become issues that need to be resolved in equipment research and development due to the widespread use of portable electronic devices and 5G networks. MXene is competent for supercapacitors and electromagnetic wave absorbers through sensible composite and microstructure design. Herein, Cu1.5Mn1.5O4 Hollow Nanosphere Decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene (CuMnHS MX) was prepared by simple electrostatic self-assembly. Hybrid membranes can be quickly prepared by vacuum-assisted filtration. CuMnHS MX exhibits excellent electromagnetic wave absorption performance and electrochemical energy storage properties. High specific capacitance (2089 mF cm2 at 2.5 mA cm2) and excellent cycle stability (99.89 after 8000 cycles) are achieved, which are attributed to the increased interlayer spacing and improved interlayer ion transport efficiency. When assembled into symmetrical flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor (SC), the device has a specific capacitance of 382.9 mF cm2 and an energy density of 53.18 μWh cm2 at a power density of 277.8 μW cm2. Meanwhile, CuMnHS MX has advantageous absorbing properties. When the thickness is 4 mm, the minimum reflection loss (RLmin) is 53.42 dB at 6.08 GHz. Adjustable absorbing property is achieved, and the absorbing energy efficiency can cover X and most C, Ku bands. These excellent EMA properties are derived from the 3D structure and rich dipole interface polarization. CuMnHS MX is a promising bifunctional material for electrochemical energy storage and electromagnetic wave absorption.
conclusion: 4 Conclusion In summary, CuMnHS decorating between MXene nanosheets can considerably enhance the electrochemical and microwave absorption capabilities of NXene. The improvements include 3D structure with rich interfaces, greater interlayer spacing, higher relaxation polarization, optimized impedance matching, and interlayer ion transport efficiency. The CuMnHS MX electrode has a specific capacitance of 2089 mF cm 2 and 99.89 high capacity retention rate after 8000 cycles. The symmetrical flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor assembled by CuMnHS MX hybrid film has a specific capacitance of 382.9 mF cm 2 and energy density of 53.18 μWh cm 2 at 277.8 μW cm 2 power density. For microwave absorption performance, when the thickness is 4 mm, the RL min of CuMnHS MX reaches 53.42 dB at 6.08 GHz. It is worth noting that CuMnHS MX has adjustable absorbing properties, and the absorbing energy efficiency can cover X and most C, Ku bands. For electrochemical energy storage and electromagnetic wave absorption, CuMnHS MX is a potentially bifunctional material.

The sediment and supernatant parts of synthesized Ti3C2Tx MXene were applied onto cotton substrates through a drop-casting technique at various concentrations to explore the influence of MXene dispersion density on the structural, morphological, and electrochemical properties of the fabric electrodes. Findings indicate that the lower-concentration dispersions not only improve the structural integrity of the coatings but also enhance their electrochemical functionality. title: Interface engineering based NiCoMoO4 Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructure for high-performance flexible supercapacitors
authors: Wei Li, Bita Farhadi, Miaomiao Liu, Peiru Wang, Jiayi Wang, Yaoyao Zhang, Guoxiang Ma, Runnan Huang, Jiayi Zhao, Kai Wang, Yao Tong
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
abstract: The advancement of interface engineering has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in overcoming the primary impediment associated with sluggish reaction kinetics in supercapacitor electrodes. In this investigation, we employed a facile co-precipitation method to synthesize NiCoMoO4 MXene heterostructures utilizing Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets as carriers. This heterostructure inhibits the restacking of MXene nanosheets and simultaneously enhances the exposure of electrochemically active sites in NiCoMoO4 nanorods, thereby mitigating the reduction in specific capacitance resulting from volumetric fluctuations. The NiCoMoO4 MXene electrode, possessing pseudo-capacitance properties, demonstrates an impressive level of specific capacitance, exceptional performance across various charging rates, and consistent behavior throughout repeated cycles. By optimizing the mass ratio, this electrode achieves a specific capacity of 1900 F g under a current density of 1 A g. Even after enduring 10,000 cycles at a significantly higher current density of 5 A g, it still maintains an impressive retention rate of 94.73 . Our density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the enhanced electrochemical performance can be attributed to the improved electronic coupling within the NiCoMoO4 MXene heterostructure. The integration of NiCoMoO4 MXene cathode and activated carbon (AC) anode with an alkaline gel electrolyte containing potassium ferricyanide in flexible quasi-solid-state supercapacitors (FSSCs) results in exceptional electrochemical performance and flexibility. These FSSCs demonstrate a maximum energy density of 72.89 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 850 W kg 1, while maintaining an impressive power output of 16,780 W kg 1 with an energy density of 37.28 Wh kg 1. Based on these outstanding properties, it is evident that the NiCoMoO4 MXene heterojunction possesses significant advantages as electrode material for supercapacitors, and the fabricated FSSCs devices pave a new pathway for flexible electronic devices.
conclusion: In conclusion, we have successfully developed NiCoMoO4 MXene heterostructure electrode materials with exceptional electrochemical properties via a facile co-precipitation method. This method effectively addresses the issue of MXene layer restacking during the preparation process. Notably, the NiCoMoO4 MXene-2 heterostructure achieves a high specific capacitance of 1900 F g at 1 A g, surpassing that of pure NiCoMoO4 (932 F g) and MXene (230 F g). It also exhibited outstanding rate performance (1290 F g at 20 A g) and excellent cyclic stability (94.73 initial capacity retention rate after 10,000 charge and discharge cycles). The electrochemical performance of the electrode materials reported in this paper outperforms that of previously reported MXene composite materials [52] ,[53] ,[54] . This remarkable performance can be attributed to the synergistic effect between the heterostructure and oxygen vacancy. Additionally, our DFT calculations demonstrate that enhanced electron coupling in the NiCoMoO4 MXene heterostructure is also responsible for its superb electrochemical performance. Impressively, the constructed NiCoMoO4 MXene AC FSSCs achieve a maximum energy density of 72.89 Wh kg 1 at power densities up to 850 W kg 1 while maintaining significant cycle stability and flexibility. Thus, this paper provides a straightforward approach for preparing MXene metal composites with high specific capacitance and long cycle stability, offering new insights into developing electrode materials with flexible and superior electrochemical properties for next-generation portable wearable electronics. title: Nitrogen-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene prepared by thermal decomposition of ammonium salts and its application in flexible quasi-solid-state supercapacitor
authors: Man Cai, Xiaochun Wei, Haifu Huang, Fulin Yuan, Cong Li, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXenes show great potential for application in flexible supercapacitors, due to their good hydrophilicity, metallic conductivity and excellent flexibility. Surface modification of the MXenes by heteroatom doping is a good strategy for adjusting the layer spacing and alleviateing various shortcomings. Herein, the ammonium salt decomposition method is shown to allow rapid nitrogen doping into Ti3C2Tx nanosheets at a low temperature of 350 C. Compared to the raw Ti3C2Tx, the nitrogen-doped Ti3C2Tx (designated N-Ti3C2Tx) shows an increased layer spacing of 1.451 nm, nitrogen doping levels of 1.42 at and a low number of residual fluorine functional groups. For the application as an electrode of supercapacitors, the N-Ti3C2Tx electrode shows an outstanding pseudocapacitance performance and mechanical flexibility, with a high specific capacitance of up to 449 F g 1 at 2 mV s 1, which is 1.4 times that of the raw Ti3C2Tx MXene (i.e., 321 F g 1). Furthermore, a quasi-solid-state symmetric supercapacitor assembled with a H2SO4-PVA gel electrolyte is shown to deliver an energy density of 9.57 Wh kg 1 at 250 W kg 1. The outstanding pseudocapacitance of the N-Ti3C2Tx is attributed to the positive effect of nitrogen doping on MXene, such as larger layer spacing and the increased number of surface active sites. The strategy presented herein also opens up a convenient and versatile approach for preparing high performance MXene Materials for energy conversion and storage.
conclusion: A simple N-doping method for Ti3 C2 Tx MXene was developed herein based on the thermal decomposition of ammonium salts. A nitrogen doping level of about 1.42 at. was obtained in the N-Ti3 C2 Tx by heat treatment with ammonium chloride at 350 C for 3h. The resulting N-Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited an excellent electrochemical performance, with a high specific capacitance of 449 F g 1 , an outstanding cyclic stability (about 80.4 retention after 8000 cycles), and a high energy density of 9.57 Wh kg 1 at a power density of 250 W kg 1 for quasi-solid-state flexible device. The capacitance improvement was attributed to the positive effect of nitrogen doping on MXene. For example, nitrogen doping increased the number of Ti3 C2 Tx surface active sites and the related defects that can enhance surface capacitive contribution, and effectively increased the interlayer spacing of the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, thereby facilitating the rapid diffusion and transmission of electrolyte ions in the electrode, and increasing the charge storage capacity and cyclic stability. The significant improvement in electrochemical performance indicates that the N-Ti3 C2 Tx can be used as a promising high-performance energy storage electrode material. The proposed thermal decomposition of ammonium salts is a simple and convenient strategy, thereby opening up a new pathway for the heteroatom doping of MXenes.

title: Cost-effective synthesis route for ultra-high purity of Ti3AlC2 MAX phase with enhanced performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene and MXene NiO composite for supercapacitor application
authors: Kapil Dev Verma, Kamal K. Kar
abstract: MXene, an emerging material with versatile properties, holds immense promise for supercapacitor applications. However, transitioning from laboratory-scale synthesis to commercial viability faces significant challenges, primarily due to the prohibitively high cost, small lifespan, and self-stacking nature. Prior attempts to lower the cost burden by employing TiO2 as impurities such as TiC, TiAl, and Ti2AlC have hindered a precursor rather than Ti TiC expensive materials. Herein, a synthesis method was presented to prepare an ultra-high pure Ti3AlC2 MAX phase using an optimized molar ratio of precursors (TiO2: Al: C), calcination process, and HCl washing. The obtained material was subsequently transformed into pure Ti3C2Tx MXene by a mild etching process that helps to sustain a long lifespan. Further, to address the restacking issue and low performance of Ti3C2Tx for supercapacitor applications, a composite of MXene NiO (MX NiO) was synthesized through bath sonication. MXene exhibits a specific capacitance of 358.5 F g 1, while MX NiO composite achieves 892 F g 1 at 1 A g 1 current density within a potential window of 0.6 0.4 V with 2 M H2SO4 electrolyte. Further, in 6 M KOH electrolyte, Ti3C2Tx and MX NiO-based symmetric supercapacitors show 171 and 461 F g 1 specific capacitance at 1 A g 1 current density. The DFT-based theoretical capacitance analysis of MAX phase, MXene, and MX NiO composite supports electrochemical results. By addressing the limitations of previous approaches, this methodology can bridge the gap between laboratory research and large-scale commercial production of MXene, thus unlocking its full potential for supercapacitor applications.
conclusion: This study introduced an optimized synthesis route that enhances the scalability and cost-effectiveness for the preparation of high-purity Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. The presence of impurities such as TiC, TiAl, and Ti2 AlC has impeded previous attempts to alleviate the cost burden by utilizing TiO2 as a precursor. It proposed an optimized synthesis method that was designed to produce an ultra-high pure Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase. The method involves the use of an optimized molar ratio of precursors (3TiO2 :6.1Al:2C), a calcination process (1350 C, 2.5 hrs dwell time), and HCl washing. The resulting material was subsequently transformed into pure MXene (Ti3 C2 Tx ) through a mild etching process, contributing to its long-term stability. In addition, a composite of MX NiO was synthesized through bath sonication to resolve the issues of restacking and the limited performance of MXene for supercapacitor applications. Utilizing Raman spectroscopy, XRD analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, UV vis spectroscopy, BET analysis, XPS analysis, and SEM imaging, the comprehensive investigation of MXene, NiO, and MX NiO demonstrates their effective fabrication. The electrical conductivity of MXene films was measured and verified by illuminating LED bulbs, thereby emphasizing their potential for electronic applications and energy storage. This study also examined the electrochemical efficacy of MXene and MX NiO-based electrodes with H2 SO4 and KOH electrolytes for supercapacitor applications. Ti3 C2 Tx MXene possesses a specific capacitance of 358.5 F g 1 . The MX NiO composite achieved a specific capacitance of 892 F g 1 within a potential window of 0.6 0.4 V when using 2 M H2 SO4 electrolyte at a current density of 1 A g 1 . These materials-based symmetric supercapacitors exhibit specific capacitances of 171 F g 1 and 461 F g 1 , respectively, at a current density of 1 A g 1 in a 6 M KOH electrolyte. Further, the DFT-based theoretical analysis of MAX phase, MXene, and MX NiO composite demonstrated superior quantum capacitance and pseudocapacitance compared to the MAX phase, attributed to their increased surface area and enhanced reactivity. This study solves the problems of MXene s high cost, short life span, and tendency to self-stack for supercapacitor applications by using inexpensive precursors, a moderate etching synthesis route, and the synthesis of MX NiO composites. title: Synthesis effect on surface functionalized Ti3C2Tx MXene supported nickel oxide nanocomposites with enhanced specific capacity for supercapacitor application
authors: Prabhakar Nikhil, S. Vasanth, N. Ponpandian, C. Viswanathan
abstract: Rich surface functionalization and active electrolyte-accessible supercapacitors are considered promising tools for enhanced energy storage capacity due to their high specific capacity and simple construction. One of the challenges in technical applications of recently developed MXene is that it causes phase transition and structural decomposition over time without delamination. Thus, a simple but effective method for increasing the stability of exfoliated MXene (Ti3C2Tx) by passivating exposed edges with Tetramethyl Ammonium Hydroxide (TMAOH) has been adopted here. In this work, we performed this delaminated MXene (DLMX) supported Nickel oxide (NiO) by three different synthesizing routes for composite preparation which have been thoroughly discussed. Bath Sonication assisted DLMX NiO was found to increase oxygen-containing surface functionalities, surface area, and uniform delivery of partner composite, enhancing the electrochemical properties compared to Solvothermal and in situ-delamination synthesis. At a current density of 1 A g, the fabricated electrode material exhibited a maximum capacity of 770C g. After 3500 cycles a remarkable cycling performance of 97.2 capacity retention and reached 88.1 after 5000 cycles at 8 A g current density. The as-assembled supercapacitor device has an energy density of up to 73 Wh kg 1 and a power density of 900 W kg 1 signifying an excellent device prospect, making them more practicable for marketable devices for advanced energy storage applications.
conclusion: An interlayer design approach using surface-functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with nickel oxide incorporation was presented using three alternative nanocomposite synthesis techniques to provide consistent, more open, and increased ionic conductive and electrochemically active space for ion transport. As an intercalant, tetramethylammonium hydroxide effectively separates neighboring exfoliated MXene sheets, increasing the ion-accessible surface area and resulting in rapid ion diffusion in several directions. By virtue of bath sonication, Nickel Oxide nanocomposite may uniformly adhere to MXene flakes, and the likelihood of fall-off is less compared to the other two approaches for enhancing electron transport. Consequently, BS- DLMX NiO at a current density of 1 A g has a reversible capacitance of 770C g and a capacitance retention of 97.2 after 3500 cycles at 8 A g, proving the existence of -OH-enhanced functional groups. MXene sheets may trap large-sized ions between interlayers and operate as space-maintaining pillars, which may increase the additional capacitance. Furthermore, symmetric supercapacitors based on BS-DLMX NiO exhibit excellent power and energy densities. The general hybrid method, which entails anchoring nanoparticles inside a 2D metallic network, might be used to develop high-performance electrodes for surface-enhanced energy storage devices. The current study proposes a way to lessen the self-restacking phenomena of Ti3 C2 Tx films without sacrificing conductivity; this approach applies to various layered electrode materials for energy storage applications with a fresh route for improved electrochemical performances.
